translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 149

sentences.zh: 【梁紀五】起屠維大淵獻，盡昭陽單閼，凡五年。

translations.literal: [Liang Records 5] From Tuxi Dayuanxian through Zhaoyang Shankuo; five years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Liang Records 5] From Tuxi Dayuanxian through Zhaoyang Shankuo—five years in all.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝五天監十八年（

translations.literal: The Martial Emperor Gaozu, eighteenth year of Tianjian (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang, eighteenth year of Tianjian (

sentences.zh: 己亥，公元五一九年）

translations.literal: jihai, corresponding to 519 CE)
translations.idiomatic: jihai, corresponding to 519 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲申，以尚書左僕射袁昂為尚書令，右僕射王暕為左僕射，太子詹事徐勉為右僕射。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on jiashen, the Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Ang was made Director of the Masters of Writing, the Right Vice Director Wang Yan was made Left Vice Director, and the Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household Xu Mian was made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on jiashen, Yuan Ang was promoted from Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing to Director; Wang Yan moved from Right to Left Vice Director; and Xu Mian, Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, became Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，魏主下詔，稱：「皇太后臨朝踐極，歲將半紀，宣稱『詔』以令宇內。」

translations.literal: On dinghai, the Northern Wei ruler issued an edict stating: "The Empress Dowager has held court and ascended the throne; nearly half a cycle of years has passed—it is fitting to proclaim 'imperial edicts' to command all within the realm."
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, the Northern Wei emperor issued an edict: "The Empress Dowager has held court and taken the throne; nearly thirty years have passed. Edicts should be issued as 'imperial edicts' to command the realm."

sentences.zh: 辛卯，上祀南郊。

translations.literal: On xinmao, the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Emperor Wu sacrificed at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 魏徵西將軍平陸文侯張彝之子仲瑀上封事，求銓削選格，排抑武人，不使豫清品。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhongyu, son of Zhang Yi, Marquis Wen of Pinglu and Western Campaign General of Wei, submitted a sealed memorial asking to trim the selection regulations and suppress military men, not allowing them to enter the pure ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongyu, son of Zhang Yi, Western Campaign General and Marquis Wen of Pinglu, submitted a sealed memorial proposing to tighten civil-service selection rules, curb military men, and bar them from the pure official grades.

sentences.zh: 於是喧謗盈路，立榜大巷，剋期會集，屠害其家；

translations.literal: Thereupon clamor and slander filled the roads; notices were posted in the great lanes fixing a date for assembly to slaughter his household;
translations.idiomatic: Clamor and abuse filled the streets; notices went up in the main thoroughfares fixing a day to gather and slaughter his household;

sentences.zh: 彝父子晏然，不以為意。

translations.literal: Father and son Yi remained serene and did not take it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi and his sons remained calm and paid it no heed.

sentences.zh: 二月，庚午，羽林、虎賁近千人相帥至尚書省詬罵，求仲瑀兄左民郎中始均不獲，以瓦石擊省門；

translations.literal: In the second month, on gengwu, nearly a thousand Imperial Guard and Tiger Guard soldiers led one another to the Masters of Writing compound to revile and abuse; seeking Zhongyu's elder brother Shi Jun, Left Section Director of the People, they did not obtain him and struck the compound gates with tiles and stones;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on gengwu, nearly a thousand Imperial Guard and Tiger Guard soldiers marched together to the Masters of Writing offices to curse and riot; they could not find Zhongyu's elder brother Shi Jun, Director in the Left Section of the People, and pelted the gates with tiles and stones;

sentences.zh: 上下懾懼，莫敢禁討。

translations.literal: High and low were terrified; none dared restrain or punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Officials high and low were terrified; no one dared stop or punish them.

sentences.zh: 遂持火掠道中薪蒿，以杖石為兵器，直造其第，曳彝堂下，捶辱極意，唱呼動地，焚其第捨。

translations.literal: They then took fire, gathered fuel and reeds along the road, used staves and stones as weapons, went straight to his residence, dragged Yi down into the hall, beat and humiliated him to the utmost, their shouts shaking the ground, and burned his buildings.
translations.idiomatic: They seized torches, gathered brushwood along the road, armed themselves with clubs and stones, marched straight to the Zhang residence, dragged Yi into the hall and beat him without mercy amid earth-shaking cries, then burned the house.

sentences.zh: 始均逾垣走，復還拜賊，請其父命，賊就毆擊，生投之火中。

translations.literal: Shi Jun climbed the wall and fled, then returned to bow to the rioters and beg for his father's life; the rioters beat him on the spot and threw him alive into the fire.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jun scaled the wall and fled, then came back to bow to the mob and plead for his father's life; they beat him and threw him alive into the flames.

sentences.zh: 仲瑀重傷走免，彝僅有餘息，再宿而死。

translations.literal: Zhongyu, badly wounded, fled and escaped; Yi had only a breath left and died after two nights.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyu escaped with grave wounds; Yi lingered two days and died.

sentences.zh: 遠近震駭。

translations.literal: Near and far were shaken with horror.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was shaken with horror.

sentences.zh: 胡太后收掩羽林、虎賁凶強者八人斬之，其餘不復窮治。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Hu seized eight fierce and violent men among the Imperial Guard and Tiger Guard and beheaded them; the rest were not further pursued.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Hu arrested eight of the ringleaders among the guards and beheaded them; the rest went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，大赦以安之，因令武官得依資入選。

translations.literal: On yihai, a general amnesty was proclaimed to pacify them, and military officers were allowed to enter selection according to seniority.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, a general amnesty was proclaimed to calm the realm, and military officers were allowed to qualify for office by seniority.

sentences.zh: 識者知魏之將亂矣。

translations.literal: Those with insight knew that Wei was about to fall into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Men of discernment knew that Northern Wei was heading toward chaos.

sentences.zh: 時官員既少，應選者多，吏部尚書李韶銓注不行，大致怨嗟；

translations.literal: At the time official posts were few and candidates many; Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Li Shao's assignments could not proceed, and there was widespread complaint;
translations.idiomatic: Posts were few and candidates many; Minister of Personnel Li Shao could not keep up with appointments, and complaints were widespread;

sentences.zh: 更以殿中尚書崔亮為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Cui Liang, Palace Secretary, was transferred to be Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretary Cui Liang was made Minister of Personnel in his place.

sentences.zh: 亮奏為格制，不問士之賢愚，專以停解月日為斷，沉滯者皆稱其能。

translations.literal: Liang memorialized to establish a regulation system, not asking whether gentlemen were worthy or foolish but taking only the month and day of leave and dismissal as the criterion; those long stalled all praised his ability.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Liang proposed a fixed rule: merit would not matter—only the date one left office would decide promotion. Everyone who had languished in the queue praised him.

sentences.zh: 亮甥司空咨議劉景安與亮書曰：「殷、周以鄉塾貢士，兩漢由州郡薦才，魏、晉因循，又置中正，雖未盡美，應什收六七。

translations.literal: Liang's nephew Liu Jing'an, Consultant of the Directorate of Works, wrote to Liang saying: "Yin and Zhou presented gentlemen through village schools; the two Han dynasties recommended talent through provinces and commanderies; Wei and Jin followed suit and also established Rectifiers—though not wholly perfect, they should have captured six or seven tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Liang's nephew Liu Jing'an, a consultant at the Directorate of Works, wrote to him: "Yin and Zhou advanced scholars through village schools; Han relied on provincial recommendation; Wei and Jin continued that and added Rectifiers of Talent—imperfect, but they surely picked up six or seven men in ten.

sentences.zh: 而朝廷貢才，止求其文，不取其理，察孝廉唯論章句，不及治道，立中正不考才行，空辯氏姓，取士之途不博，沙汰之理未精。

translations.literal: Yet when the court presented talent it sought only literary skill, not substance; in examining Filial and Incorrupt candidates it discussed only textual glosses, not governance; in establishing Rectifiers it did not examine ability and conduct but argued only over clan names—the paths to obtain gentlemen were not broad, and the principles of sifting were not refined.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court now prizes literary polish over substance, examines Filial and Incorrupt men on glosses rather than governance, and lets Rectifiers debate pedigree instead of talent—narrow roads to office and crude screening.

sentences.zh: 舅屬當銓衡，宜須改張易調，如何反為停年格以限之，天下士子誰復修厲名行哉！」

translations.literal: Uncle, holding the scales of selection, ought to change and adjust—how can you instead make a seniority grid to limit them? Which gentleman under heaven will still cultivate and sharpen fame and conduct!"
translations.idiomatic: You hold the scales of appointment—you should reform the system. Why impose a seniority grid instead? What scholar will still strive for virtue and reputation?"

sentences.zh: 亮復書曰：「汝所言乃有深致。

translations.literal: Liang replied: "What you say has deep meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Liang wrote back: "Your words have real depth.

sentences.zh: 吾昨為此格，有由而然。

translations.literal: I made this grid yesterday for reasons that made it so.
translations.idiomatic: I adopted this rule yesterday for good reason.

sentences.zh: 古今不同，時宜須異。

translations.literal: Ancient and modern differ; the times require what is different.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient and modern times differ; policy must change with them.

sentences.zh: 昔子產鑄刑書以救弊，叔向譏之以正法，何異汝以古禮難權宜哉！」

translations.literal: Formerly Zichan cast penal statutes to remedy abuses, and Shuxiang mocked him for violating proper law—how is that different from your using ancient rites to challenge expedient measures!"
translations.idiomatic: When Zichan cast the penal code to cure abuses, Shuxiang mocked him for violating orthodoxy—how is your appeal to ancient rites against my expedient any different?"

sentences.zh: 洛陽令代人薛琡上書，言：「黎元之命，繫於長吏，若以選曹唯取年勞，不簡能否，義均行雁，次若貫魚，執簿呼名，一吏足矣，數人而用，何謂銓衡！」

translations.literal: Xue Fan of Dai, Magistrate of Luoyang, submitted a memorial saying: "The lives of the common people depend on chief officials. If the Selection Bureau takes only years of service and does not sift ability, it is like geese in a row and fish on a string—calling names from the register: one clerk would suffice. What is the use of many men—what does 'weighing the scales' mean!"
translations.idiomatic: Xue Fan, magistrate of Luoyang, memorialized: "The people's fate rests with local magistrates. If the Selection Bureau promotes only by seniority and ignores ability, appointments march like geese in flight or fish on a string—one clerk with a roster could do the job. Why keep a whole bureau to 'weigh' candidates?"

sentences.zh: 書奏，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; no response was given.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received; the court did not reply.

sentences.zh: 後因請見，復奏「乞令王公貴臣薦賢以補郡縣。」

translations.literal: Later, on requesting an audience, he again memorialized: "I beg that kings, dukes, and noble ministers recommend the worthy to fill commanderies and counties."
translations.idiomatic: Later, seeking an audience, he again asked "that princes and great ministers recommend the worthy to fill county and commandery posts."

sentences.zh: 詔公卿議之，事亦寢。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the high ministers to discuss it; the matter also lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the high ministers to discuss it; the proposal died there too.

sentences.zh: 其後甄琛等繼亮為吏部尚書，利其便己，踵而行之。

translations.literal: Thereafter Zhen Chen and others succeeded Liang as Minister of the Ministry of Personnel; finding it convenient for themselves, they followed in his footsteps.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhen Chen and others succeeded Cui Liang as Minister of Personnel; finding the rule convenient, they kept it.

sentences.zh: 魏之選舉失人，自亮始也。

translations.literal: Wei's selection losing the right men began with Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei's decline in choosing officials began with Cui Liang.

sentences.zh: 初，燕燕郡太守高湖奔魏，其子謐為侍御史，坐法徙懷朔鎮，世居北邊，遂習鮮卑之俗。

translations.literal: Earlier, Gao Hu, Administrator of Yan Commandery, fled to Wei; his son Mi became Attending Censor, was punished by law and exiled to Huaishuo Garrison, and for generations dwelt on the northern frontier, thus learning Xianbei customs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Gao Hu, governor of Yan Commandery, defected to Wei. His son Mi became an attending censor, was punished and exiled to Huaishuo Garrison; the family lived on the frontier for generations and adopted Xianbei ways.

sentences.zh: 謐孫歡，沉深有大志，家貧，執役在平城，富人婁氏女見而奇之，遂嫁焉。

translations.literal: Mi's grandson Huan was deep and reserved with great ambition; his family was poor and he performed corvée labor at Pingcheng. A rich man's daughter of the Lou clan saw him and found him remarkable, and married him.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's grandson Gao Huan was reserved and ambitious. Poor, he did corvée labor at Pingcheng; a wealthy Lou clansman's daughter saw him, marveled at him, and married him.

sentences.zh: 始有馬，得給鎮為函使，至洛陽，見張彝之死，還家，傾貲以結客。

translations.literal: When he first had a horse he was assigned to the garrison as a courier, went to Luoyang, saw Zhang Yi's death, returned home, and poured out his assets to gather clients.
translations.idiomatic: Once he owned a horse he served the garrison as a courier. In Luoyang he witnessed Zhang Yi's murder; back home he spent his fortune recruiting followers.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，歡曰：「宿衛相帥焚大臣之第，朝廷懼其亂而不問，為政如此，事可知矣，財物豈可常守邪！」

translations.literal: Someone asked the reason; Huan said: "Palace guards led one another to burn a great minister's residence; the court feared their disorder and did not inquire. With government like this, affairs can be known—how can wealth be permanently kept!"
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, Gao Huan said: "Guards burned a minister's house and the court, afraid of riot, did nothing. When rule is like that, the end is clear—who can keep his wealth forever?"

sentences.zh: 歡與懷朔省事雲中司馬子如、秀容劉貴、中山賈顯智、戶曹史咸陽孫騰、外兵史懷朔侯景、獄掾善無尉景、廣寧蔡俊特相友善，並以任俠雄於鄉里。

translations.literal: Huan was especially friendly with Sima Ziru of Yunzhong, an aide at Huaishuo; Liu Gui of Xiurong; Jia Xianzhi of Zhongshan; Sun Teng of Xianyang, clerk of the Household Section; Hou Jing of Huaishuo, clerk of External Troops; Wei Jing of Shanyang, prison clerk; and Cai Jun of Guangning—all chivalrous and dominant in their home districts.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan grew especially close to Sima Ziru, Liu Gui, Jia Xianzhi, Sun Teng, Hou Jing, Wei Jing, and Cai Jun—all men of reckless valor who dominated their neighborhoods.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁巳，大赦。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on dingsi, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on dingsi, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 五月，戊戌，魏以任城王澄為司徒，京光王繼為司空。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on wuxu, Wei made Prince Cheng of Rencheng Grand Minister and Prince Ji of Jingguang Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on wuxu, Northern Wei appointed Prince Cheng of Rencheng Grand Minister and Prince Ji of Jingguang Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 魏累世強盛，東夷、西域貢獻不絕，又立互市以致南貨，至是府庫盈溢。

translations.literal: Wei had been strong for successive generations; tribute from the eastern Yi and Western Regions was unceasing, and mutual markets were established to bring in southern goods—by this time the treasuries overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: For generations Northern Wei had been mighty; eastern and western peoples sent tribute without cease, and frontier markets brought southern goods—now the treasuries overflowed.

sentences.zh: 胡太后嘗幸絹藏，命王公嬪主從行者百餘人各自負絹，稱力取之，少者不減百餘匹。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Hu once visited the silk storehouse and ordered more than a hundred kings, dukes, consorts, and ladies in attendance each to carry silk away, taking as much as their strength allowed—none took fewer than a hundred bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Hu once visited the silk vault and told the hundred-odd princes, consorts, and ladies in her train to carry off silk by strength; even the weakest took more than a hundred bolts.

sentences.zh: 尚書令、儀同三司李崇，章武王融，負絹過重，顛仆於地，崇傷腰，融損足，太后奪其絹，使空出，時人笑之。

translations.literal: Li Chong, Director of the Masters of Writing and Bearer of the Three Insignia; and Prince Rong of Zhangwu, carried silk too heavy, fell headlong to the ground—Chong injured his waist, Rong hurt his foot. The empress dowager confiscated their silk and made them leave empty-handed; people of the time laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Prince Rong of Zhangwu loaded too much silk, fell, and injured back and foot. The empress dowager seized their silk and sent them away empty-handed—a laughingstock.

sentences.zh: 融，太洛之子也。

translations.literal: Rong was the son of Tailuo.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was a son of Prince Tailuo.

sentences.zh: 侍中崔光止取兩匹，太后怪其少；

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang took only two bolts; the empress dowager wondered at how few;
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang took only two bolts; the empress dowager thought that too few;

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣兩手唯堪兩匹。」

translations.literal: he replied: "Your servant's two hands can bear only two bolts."
translations.idiomatic: he replied, "These two hands can manage only two bolts."

sentences.zh: 眾皆愧之。

translations.literal: All were ashamed before him.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone else was shamed.

sentences.zh: 時宗室外戚權幸之臣，競為豪侈。

translations.literal: At the time imperial clansmen, maternal kin, and favored ministers vied in extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes, empress kin, and favored ministers vied in extravagance.

sentences.zh: 高陽王雍，富貴冠一國，宮室園圃，侔於禁苑，僮僕六千，伎女五百，出則儀衛塞道路，歸則歌吹連日夜，一食直錢數萬。

translations.literal: Prince Yong of Gaoyang—wealth and honor foremost in the realm, palaces and gardens rivaling the imperial park, six thousand servants, five hundred singing girls; going out, guards filled the roads; returning, music and song day and night—a single meal cost tens of thousands in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong of Gaoyang was the richest man in the realm: estates rivaling the imperial park, six thousand servants, five hundred entertainers; his escort blocked the streets when he went out, and feasting ran day and night at home—a single meal cost tens of thousands of cash.

sentences.zh: 李崇富埒於雍，而性儉嗇，嘗謂人曰：「高陽一食，敵我千日。」

translations.literal: Li Chong's wealth matched Yong's, but his nature was frugal and stingy; he once told others: "One meal of Gaoyang equals a thousand days of mine."
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong was as rich as Prince Yong but miserly; he once said, "One of Gaoyang's meals equals a thousand days of mine."

sentences.zh: 河間王琛，每欲與雍爭富，駿馬十餘匹，皆以銀為槽，窗戶之上，玉鳳銜鈴，金龍吐旆。

translations.literal: Prince Chen of Hejian always wished to vie in wealth with Yong; more than ten fine horses all had silver mangers; above the windows jade phoenixes held bells and golden dragons spat pennants.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chen of Hejian constantly tried to outshine Prince Yong: a dozen thoroughbreds with silver mangers, jade phoenixes with bells above the windows, golden dragons spitting pennants.

sentences.zh: 嘗會諸王宴飲，酒器有水精鋒，馬腦碗，赤玉卮，製作精巧，皆中國所無。

translations.literal: Once he gathered the princes for a banquet; wine vessels included crystal goblets, agate bowls, and red jade cups—exquisitely made, all unknown in China.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet for the princes he set out crystal goblets, agate bowls, and red jade cups—finery unknown in the Central States.

sentences.zh: 又陳女樂、名馬及諸奇寶，復引諸王歷觀府庫，金錢、繒布，不可勝計。

translations.literal: He also displayed female musicians, famous horses, and various rare treasures, then led the princes through his treasuries—gold, cash, and silk brocade beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He paraded musicians, famous horses, and curios, then led the princes through his treasuries piled with gold, coin, and brocade beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 顧謂章武王融曰：「不恨我不見石崇，恨石崇不見我。」

translations.literal: Turning to Prince Rong of Zhangwu he said: "I do not regret that I never saw Shi Chong—I regret that Shi Chong never saw me."
translations.idiomatic: He told Prince Rong of Zhangwu, "I do not regret missing Shi Chong—I regret that Shi Chong never saw me."

sentences.zh: 融素以富自負，歸而惋歎，臥疾三日。

translations.literal: Rong had always prided himself on wealth; returning home he sighed in regret and took to his bed ill for three days.
translations.idiomatic: Rong, who had always prided himself on wealth, went home in despair and kept his bed three days.

sentences.zh: 京光王繼聞而省之，謂曰：「卿之貨財計不減於彼，何為愧羨乃爾？」

translations.literal: Prince Ji of Jingguang heard and visited him, saying: "Your goods and wealth surely are not less than his—why such ashamed envy?"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ji of Jingguang visited him and said, "Your fortune is surely no less than his—why envy him so?"

sentences.zh: 融曰：「始謂富於我者獨高陽耳，不意復有河間！」

translations.literal: Rong said: "At first I thought only Gaoyang was richer than I—I did not expect Hejian as well!"
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "I thought only Gaoyang outdid me—I never dreamed of Hejian!"

sentences.zh: 繼曰：「卿似袁術在淮南，不知世間復有劉備耳！」

translations.literal: Ji said: "You are like Yuan Shu in Huainan, not knowing that Liu Bei still existed in the world!"
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "You are Yuan Shu in Huainan, unaware that Liu Bei still walked the earth!"

sentences.zh: 融乃笑而起。

translations.literal: Rong then laughed and rose.
translations.idiomatic: Rong laughed and got up.

sentences.zh: 太皇好佛，營建諸寺，無復窮已，令諸州各建五級浮圖，民力疲弊。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress favored Buddhism, built temples without end, ordered each province to erect five-story pagodas, and the people's strength was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress favored Buddhism, built temples without end, and ordered every province to erect five-story pagodas until the people were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 諸王、貴人、宦官、羽林各建寺於洛陽，相高以壯麗。

translations.literal: Princes, nobles, eunuchs, and Imperial Guards each built temples in Luoyang, vying in grandeur and splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Princes, nobles, eunuchs, and guards each built Luoyang temples, competing in grandeur.

sentences.zh: 太后數設齋會，施僧物動以萬計，賞賜左右無節，所費不貲，而未嘗施惠及民。

translations.literal: The empress dowager often held vegetarian feasts; gifts to monks ran to tens of thousands; rewards to attendants were unbounded—the expense was incalculable—yet she never extended bounty to the people.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager held endless Buddhist feasts, gave monks gifts by the ten thousand, and lavished her attendants without limit—yet never aided the common people.

sentences.zh: 府庫漸虛，乃減削百官祿力。

translations.literal: As the treasuries gradually emptied, salaries and corvée allotments of the hundred offices were cut.
translations.idiomatic: Treasuries emptied, and official salaries and corvée allotments were cut.

sentences.zh: 任城王澄上表，以為：「蕭衍常蓄窺覦之志，宜及國家強盛，將士施力，早圖混壹之功。

translations.literal: Prince Cheng of Rencheng submitted a memorial, holding: "Xiao Yan constantly harbors designs of covetous watching; one should, while the state is strong and generals and soldiers exert their strength, early plan the achievement of unification.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cheng of Rencheng memorialized: "Xiao Yan of Liang constantly eyes our realm. While the state is strong and the army willing, we should seize unification early.

sentences.zh: 比年以來，公私貧困，宜節省浮費以周急務。」

translations.literal: In recent years public and private are impoverished; one should economize floating expenses to meet urgent affairs."
translations.idiomatic: In recent years public and private coffers have run dry—we should cut waste and meet urgent needs."

sentences.zh: 太后雖不能用，常優禮之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager, though she could not employ his advice, always treated him with exceptional courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager could not follow his advice but always honored him.

sentences.zh: 魏自永平以來，營明堂、壁雍，役者多不過千人，有司復藉以修寺及供它役，十餘年竟不能成。

translations.literal: Since Yongping, Wei had worked on the Bright Hall and Imperial Academy; corvée laborers were often no more than a thousand, but the relevant offices again borrowed them to repair temples and supply other tasks—after more than ten years they still could not be completed.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Yongping era Northern Wei had labored on the Bright Hall and Imperial Academy with no more than a thousand workers at a time, yet officials kept diverting them to temples and other projects—after more than ten years nothing was finished.

sentences.zh: 起部郎源子恭上書，以為：「廢經國之務，資不急之費，宜徹減諸役，早圖就功，使祖宗有嚴配之期，蒼生睹禮樂之富。」

translations.literal: Yuan Zigong, Gentleman of the Construction Section, submitted a memorial holding: "Abandoning affairs that govern the state to fund unurgent expenses—one should drastically reduce the various corvées and early plan completion, so that the ancestors have the season of solemn sacrifice and the common people behold the fullness of ritual and music."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zigong of the Construction Section wrote: "We neglect statecraft for needless spending. Cut the corvée, finish these halls, let the ancestors receive proper sacrifice, and let the people see ritual and music restored."

sentences.zh: 詔從之，然亦不能成也。

translations.literal: An edict followed his advice, yet they still could not complete them.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed—and still could not finish them.

sentences.zh: 魏人陳仲儒請依京房立准以調八音。

translations.literal: Chen Zhongru of Wei asked to follow Jing Fang in establishing the pitch-standard to tune the eight sounds.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhongru of Wei asked to follow Jing Fang's method and erect a pitch-standard to tune the eight tones.

sentences.zh: 有司詰仲儒：「京房律准，今雖有其器，曉之者鮮。

translations.literal: The relevant offices questioned Zhongru: "Jing Fang's pitch pipes and standard—though the instrument exists today, those who understand it are few.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities questioned him: "Jing Fang's pitch pipes and standard exist, but almost no one understands them.

sentences.zh: 仲儒所受何師，出何典籍？」

translations.literal: From what teacher did Zhongru receive instruction, and from what classic does it come?"
translations.idiomatic: Who was your teacher, and what text is your source?"

sentences.zh: 仲儒對言：「性頗愛琴，又嘗讀司馬彪《續漢書》，見京房准術，成數昺然。

translations.literal: Zhongru replied: "By nature I rather love the zither; I have also read Sima Biao's Book of Han Continued and saw Jing Fang's standard technique—the completed numbers are brilliantly clear.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhongru answered: "I love the zither, and in Sima Biao's Book of Han Continued I found Jing Fang's standard method—the ratios are perfectly clear.

sentences.zh: 遂竭愚思，鑽研甚久，頗有所得。

translations.literal: I then exhausted foolish thought and studied deeply for long, and gained considerably.
translations.idiomatic: I studied it long and believe I understand it well.

sentences.zh: 夫准者本以代律，取其分數，調校樂器。

translations.literal: The standard fundamentally substitutes for the pitch pipes, taking their fractional ratios to tune and adjust instruments.
translations.idiomatic: The standard replaces the pitch pipes: from its ratios one tunes instruments.

sentences.zh: 竊尋調聲之體，宮、商宜濁，征、羽用清。

translations.literal: Privately I consider the body of tuning sound: gong and shang should be thick, zhi and yu should use clarity.
translations.idiomatic: In tuning, gong and shang should be lower, zhi and yu higher.

sentences.zh: 若依公孫崇，止以十二律聲，而雲還相為宮，清濁悉足。

translations.literal: If one follows Gongsun Chong, using only the twelve pitch-pipe tones yet claiming they cyclically serve as gong, thick and clear would all suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Chong claimed the twelve pipes alone, cycling as tonic, would supply every pitch—but that cannot work.

sentences.zh: 唯黃鐘管最長，故以黃鐘為宮，則往往相順。

translations.literal: Only the huangzhong pipe is longest; thus taking huangzhong as gong, things often accord.
translations.idiomatic: Only the huangzhong pipe is longest; as tonic it often fits.

sentences.zh: 若均之八音，猶須錯采眾音，配成其美。

translations.literal: If one equalizes the eight sounds, one must still blend many tones to match and complete the beauty.
translations.idiomatic: To balance the eight timbres you must blend many notes into harmony.

sentences.zh: 若以應鐘為宮，蕤賓為征，則征濁而宮清，雖有其韻，不成音曲。

translations.literal: If one takes yingzhong as gong and ruibin as zhi, then zhi is thick and gong clear—though there is resonance, it does not form a musical piece.
translations.idiomatic: Take yingzhong as tonic and ruibin as dominant and the dominant is flat while the tonic is sharp—there may be resonance, but no real melody.

sentences.zh: 若以中呂為宮，則十二律中全無所取。

translations.literal: If one takes zhonglü as gong, then among the twelve pipes nothing at all can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Make zhonglü the tonic and none of the twelve pipes will serve.

sentences.zh: 今依京房書，中呂為宮，乃以去滅為商，執始為征，然後方韻。

translations.literal: Now following Jing Fang's book, with zhonglü as gong one takes qumie as shang and zhishi as zhi—only then is there proper resonance.
translations.idiomatic: Per Jing Fang, with zhonglü as tonic you take qumie as second and zhishi as dominant—only then do the tones agree.

sentences.zh: 而崇乃以中呂為宮，猶用林鐘為征，何由可諧！

translations.literal: Yet Chong takes zhonglü as gong yet still uses linzhong as zhi—how can it harmonize!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chong used zhonglü as tonic and linzhong as dominant—how could that harmonize!

sentences.zh: 但音聲精微，史傳簡略，舊志准十三弦，隱間九尺，不言須柱以不。

translations.literal: But sound is subtle; histories and transmissions are brief. Old records say the standard has thirteen strings, hidden within nine feet, and do not say whether posts are needed or not.
translations.idiomatic: Sound is subtle and the records terse: old texts say the standard has thirteen strings within nine feet but do not say whether it needs movable bridges.

sentences.zh: 又，一寸之內有萬九千六百八十三分，微細難明。

translations.literal: Moreover, within one inch there are 19,683 parts—subtle and hard to clarify.
translations.idiomatic: Within one inch lie 19,683 fractional parts—too fine to see clearly.

sentences.zh: 仲儒私曾考驗，准當施柱，但前卻柱中，以約准分，則相生之韻已自應合。

translations.literal: Zhongru privately once tested: the standard should have posts applied; only moving the posts forward and back within to approximate the standard's divisions, then the mutually generating resonance already accords of itself.
translations.idiomatic: I have tested it: the standard needs bridges; sliding them along the middle string to mark the ratios makes the generating fifths fall into place.

sentences.zh: 其中弦粗細，須與琴宮相類，施軫以調聲，令與黃鐘相合。

translations.literal: The middle string's thickness must resemble the zither's gong string; tuning pegs are applied to adjust sound so it matches huangzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The middle string should match the zither's lowest string; pegs tune it to huangzhong.

sentences.zh: 中弦下依數畫六十律清濁之節，其餘十二弦須施柱如箏，即於中弦案盡一週之聲，度著十二弦上。

translations.literal: Below the middle string, according to the numbers, mark the nodes of thick and clear for the sixty pitches; the other twelve strings must have posts applied like a zheng—then on the middle string lay out the full cycle of sounds and transfer them onto the twelve strings.
translations.idiomatic: Mark the sixty pitch nodes under the middle string; set bridges on the other twelve strings as on a zheng, take the full octave on the middle string, and transfer those positions to the rest.

sentences.zh: 然後依相生之法，以次運行，取十二律之商、征。

translations.literal: Then following the method of mutual generation, run in sequence to obtain shang and zhi of the twelve pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Then by the generating cycle derive the second and dominant of each of the twelve pipes in turn.

sentences.zh: 商、征既定，又依琴五調調聲之法以均樂器，然後錯采眾聲以文飾之，若事有乖此，聲則不和。

translations.literal: Once shang and zhi are fixed, again follow the zither's five-mode method of tuning sound to equalize instruments; then blend many sounds to ornament them—if affairs depart from this, the sound will not harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: With second and dominant fixed, tune other instruments by the zither's five modes, then blend tones into ornament—deviate from this and harmony fails.

sentences.zh: 且燧人不師資而習火，延壽不束修以變律，故雲知之者欲教而無從，心達者體知而無師，苟有一毫所得，皆關心抱，豈必要經師受然後為奇哉！」

translations.literal: Moreover, Suiren did not rely on a teacher to learn fire; Zhong Zhongyou did not present bundles of silk to change pitch—thus it is said those who know wish to teach yet have none to follow, those whose hearts penetrate embody knowledge yet have no master. If one gains even a hair's breadth, it all concerns the heart's embrace—must one necessarily receive instruction from a canonical master before becoming remarkable!"
translations.idiomatic: Suiren learned fire without a teacher; Zhong Zhongyou changed pitch without a formal pupil. True knowledge cannot always be taught, nor mastery always inherited—any genuine insight comes from the heart. Must one have a canonical master to matter?"

sentences.zh: 尚書蕭寶寅奏：仲儒學不師受，輕欲製作，不合依許，事遂寢。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Xiao Baoyin memorialized: Zhongru's learning has no teacher's transmission; he lightly wishes to manufacture—he should not be approved. The affair lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Director Xiao Baoyin objected that Chen Zhongru had no teacher and rashly wished to invent—the court refused, and the project died.

sentences.zh: 魏中尉東平王匡以論議數為任城王澄所奪，憤恚，復治其故棺，欲奏攻澄。

translations.literal: Kuang, Prince of Dongping and Commandant of Wei, because his discourse was repeatedly seized by Prince Cheng of Rencheng, was resentful and angry; he refurbished his old coffin and wished to memorialize attacking Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kuang of Dongping, Commandant of Wei, resented Prince Cheng of Rencheng for repeatedly winning debates against him; he refurbished his old coffin and planned to impeach Cheng.

sentences.zh: 澄因奏匡罪狀三十餘條，廷尉處以死刑。

translations.literal: Cheng thereupon memorialized more than thirty counts of Kuang's crimes; the Minister of Justice sentenced him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng struck first with a memorial listing more than thirty charges; the Minister of Justice sentenced Kuang to death.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，己未，詔免死，削除官爵，以車騎將軍侯剛代領中尉。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on jiwei, an edict spared death, stripped office and rank, and made General of Chariots and Cavalry Hou Gang acting Commandant in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on jiwei, an edict spared his life, stripped his rank, and made General Hou Gang acting Commandant.

sentences.zh: 三公郎中辛雄奏理匡，以為：「歷奏三朝，骨鯁之跡，朝野具知，故高祖賜名曰匡。

translations.literal: Xin Xiong, Gentleman of the Three Excellencies, memorialized on Kuang's behalf, holding: "He has memorialized through three reigns; his blunt and upright traces are known to court and countryside—therefore Gaozu bestowed the name Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Xiong of the Three Excellencies pleaded for Kuang: "He has served three reigns with blunt honesty known to all—the founding emperor named him Kuang for that very quality.

sentences.zh: 先帝已容之於前，陛下亦宜寬之於後，若終貶黜，恐杜忠臣之口。」

translations.literal: The late emperor already showed forbearance before; Your Majesty should also show lenience afterward—if he is finally demoted and dismissed, I fear the mouths of loyal ministers will be stopped."
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor already spared him once; Your Majesty should show mercy again—final banishment would silence every loyal voice."

sentences.zh: 未幾，復除匡平州刺史。

translations.literal: Not long after, Kuang was again appointed Governor of Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Kuang was reappointed Governor of Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 雄，琛之族孫也。

translations.literal: Xiong was a collateral descendant of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Xiong was a collateral descendant of the Chen clan.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚寅，胡太后游嵩高；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on gengyin, Empress Dowager Hu toured Songgao;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on gengyin, Empress Dowager Hu visited Mount Song;

sentences.zh: 癸巳，還宮。

translations.literal: On guisi, she returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi she returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 太后從容謂兼中書舍人楊昱曰：「親姻在外，不稱人心，卿有聞，慎勿諱隱！」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager, at her ease, said to Acting Palace Secretary Yang Yu: "Kinsmen abroad do not accord with people's hearts—if you hear anything, take care not to conceal it!"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said calmly to Acting Palace Secretary Yang Yu: "My kin abroad have lost the people's trust—if you hear anything, do not hide it from me!"

sentences.zh: 昱奏揚州刺史李崇五車載貨，恆州刺史楊鈞造銀食器，餉領軍元義。

translations.literal: Yu memorialized that Yangzhou Governor Li Chong had five cartloads of goods, Hengzhou Governor Yang Jun had made silver tableware, and both presented gifts to Commander of the Guards Yuan Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yu reported that Governor Li Chong of Yangzhou had sent five cartloads of goods, Governor Yang Jun of Hengzhou had had silver tableware made, and both had presented gifts to Commander Yuan Yi.

sentences.zh: 太后召義夫妻，泣而責之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager summoned Yuan Yi and his wife, wept, and rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager summoned Yuan Yi and his wife, wept, and rebuked them.

sentences.zh: 義由是怨昱。

translations.literal: Yuan Yi thereupon resented Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi bore a grudge against Yang Yu from that day on.

sentences.zh: 昱叔父舒妻，武昌王和之妹也。

translations.literal: The wife of Yu's uncle Shu was the younger sister of Prince He of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of Yang Yu's uncle Shu was a younger sister of Prince He of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 和即義之從祖。

translations.literal: He was Yuan Yi's great-uncle on the collateral line.
translations.idiomatic: He was Yuan Yi's grand-uncle in the collateral line.

sentences.zh: 舒卒，元氏頻請別居，昱父椿泣責不聽，元氏恨之。

translations.literal: When Shu died, the Yuan clan woman repeatedly asked to live apart; Yu's father Chun wept and rebuked her but would not listen—the Yuan woman resented this.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu died, the Yuan woman repeatedly demanded a separate household; Yang Yu's father Chun wept and scolded her but would not yield, and she came to hate him.

sentences.zh: 會瀛州民劉宣明謀反，事覺，逃亡。

translations.literal: It happened that Liu Xuanming of Yingzhou plotted rebellion; the affair was discovered, and he fled.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Liu Xuanming of Yingzhou plotted rebellion; the plot was exposed and he fled.

sentences.zh: 義使和及元氏誣告昱藏匿宣明，且云：「昱父定州刺史椿，叔父華州刺史津，並送甲仗三百具，謀為不逞。」

translations.literal: Yuan Yi had He and the Yuan woman falsely accuse Yu of harboring Xuanming, and further said: "Yu's father Chun, Governor of Dingzhou, and his uncle Jin, Governor of Huazhou, each sent three hundred suits of armor and weapons, plotting mischief."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi had He and the Yuan woman accuse Yang Yu of hiding Xuanming, alleging that Yang Yu's father Chun, Governor of Dingzhou, and his uncle Jin, Governor of Huazhou, had each sent three hundred sets of arms and armor in a plot of sedition."

sentences.zh: 義復構成之。

translations.literal: Yuan Yi further fabricated the case.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi fabricated the charges as well.

sentences.zh: 遣御杖五百人夜圍昱宅，收之，一無所獲。

translations.literal: He sent five hundred imperial staff-bearers by night to surround Yu's residence and seize him; nothing at all was found.
translations.idiomatic: He sent five hundred imperial guards by night to surround Yang Yu's house and arrest him, but found nothing.

sentences.zh: 太后問其狀，昱具對為元氏所怨。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager asked the circumstances; Yu answered fully that he was resented by the Yuan woman.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager asked what had happened; Yang Yu explained in full that the Yuan woman bore him a grudge.

sentences.zh: 太后解昱縛，處和及元氏死刑，既而義營救之，和直免官，元氏竟不坐。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager released Yu's bonds, sentenced He and the Yuan woman to death; afterward Yuan Yi intervened to save them—He was merely stripped of office, and the Yuan woman in the end was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager freed Yang Yu and sentenced He and the Yuan woman to death; Yuan Yi then intervened—He was only dismissed from office, and the Yuan woman was never punished at all.

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，癸丑，魏任城文宣王澄卒。

translations.literal: In winter, the twelfth month, on guichou, Prince Wensuan Cheng of Rencheng of Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the twelfth month, on guichou, Prince Cheng of Rencheng, posthumously Wensuan, died.

sentences.zh: 庚申，魏大赦。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Wei proclaimed a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Northern Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 是歲，高句麗王雲座，世子安立。

translations.literal: That year, King Yun of Goguryeo took the throne; the heir An was installed.
translations.idiomatic: That year King Yun of Goguryeo ascended the throne and his heir An was installed.

sentences.zh: 魏以郎選不精，大加沙汰，唯朱元旭、辛雄、羊深、源子恭及范陽祖瑩等八人以才用見留，餘皆罷遣。

translations.literal: Wei, because selection of gentlemen was not refined, greatly winnowed them; only Zhu Yuanxu, Xin Xiong, Yang Shen, Yuan Zigong, and Zu Ying of Fanyang among eight men were kept for talent and capacity—the rest were all dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Because civil-service selection had grown lax, Northern Wei conducted a major purge; only eight men of proven talent were retained—Zhu Yuanxu, Xin Xiong, Yang Shen, Yuan Zigong, and Zu Ying of Fanyang among them—and all the rest were sent home.

sentences.zh: 深，祉之子也。

translations.literal: Shen was the son of Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shen was the son of Zhi.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝五普通元年（

translations.literal: The Martial Emperor Gaozu, first year of Putong (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang, first year of Putong (

sentences.zh: 庚子，公元五二零年）

translations.literal: gengzi, corresponding to the year 520 CE)
translations.idiomatic: gengzi, corresponding to 520 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙亥朔，改元，大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the yihai new moon, the era name was changed and a great amnesty proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the new moon of the first month, yihai, the era name was changed and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 丙子，日有食之。

translations.literal: On bingzi, the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 己卯，以臨川王宏為太尉、揚州刺史，金紫光祿大夫王份為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: On jimao, Prince Hong of Linchuan was made Grand Marshal and Governor of Yangzhou; Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal Wang Fen was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Prince Hong of Linchuan was appointed Grand Marshal and Governor of Yangzhou, and Wang Fen, Grand Master with the Golden Seal of Imperial Splendor, became Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 份，奐之弟也。

translations.literal: Fen was the younger brother of Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fen was the younger brother of Wang Huan.

sentences.zh: 左軍將軍豫寧威伯馮道根卒。

translations.literal: General of the Left Army Feng Daogen, Marquis Wei of Yuning, died.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Daogen, General of the Left Army and Marquis Wei of Yuning, died.

sentences.zh: 是日上春，祠二廟，既出宮，有司以聞。

translations.literal: That day was the spring ceremony; the two ancestral temples were sacrificed to. After the emperor had left the palace, the relevant offices reported it.
translations.idiomatic: That day was the spring ancestral rite at the two temples. After the emperor had left the palace, the officials reported the death.

sentences.zh: 上問中書舍人朱異曰：「吉凶同日，今可行乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked Palace Secretary Zhu Yi: "Auspicious and inauspicious affairs fall on the same day—may we proceed now?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Palace Secretary Zhu Yi: "Joy and mourning fall on the same day—may the rite still proceed?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「昔衛獻公聞柳莊死，不釋祭服而往。

translations.literal: He replied: "Formerly Duke Xian of Wei, hearing that Liu Zhuang had died, did not remove his sacrificial robes but went at once.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "When Duke Xian of Wei heard that Liu Zhuang had died, he went without laying aside his sacrificial robes.

sentences.zh: 道根雖未為社稷之臣，亦有勞王室，臨之，禮也。」

translations.literal: Daogen, though not yet a minister of the altars of soil and grain, also had labors for the royal house—to go to him is ritual propriety."
translations.idiomatic: Daogen was not yet a pillar of the state, but he had served the dynasty well; to attend his house is only proper."

sentences.zh: 上即幸其宅，哭之以慟。

translations.literal: The emperor at once visited his residence and wept for him with deep grief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went straight to his house and wept for him in anguish.

sentences.zh: 高句麗世子安遣使入貢。

translations.literal: An, heir of Goguryeo, sent envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: An, crown prince of Goguryeo, sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 二月，癸丑，以安為寧東將軍、高句麗王，遣使者江法盛授安衣冠劍佩。

translations.literal: In the second month, on guichou, An was made General Who Pacifies the East and King of Goguryeo; the envoy Jiang Fasheng was sent to invest An with robes, cap, sword, and girdle pendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on guichou, An was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and King of Goguryeo; the envoy Jiang Fasheng was dispatched to invest him with robes, regalia, sword, and girdle ornaments.

sentences.zh: 魏光州兵就海中執之，送洛陽。

translations.literal: Wei troops of Guangzhou seized him at sea and sent him to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei troops from Guangzhou seized him at sea and escorted him to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 魏太傅、侍中、清河文獻王懌，美風儀，胡太后逼而幸之。

translations.literal: Yuan Yi, Grand Tutor, Palace Attendant, and Prince of Qinghe the Cultured and Illustrious of Wei, had fine bearing and grace; Empress Dowager Hu forced him and favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi, Prince of Qinghe, Grand Tutor and Palace Attendant of Northern Wei, was a man of striking presence; Empress Dowager Hu forced herself upon him.

sentences.zh: 然素有才能，輔政多所匡益，好文學，禮敬士人，時望甚重。

translations.literal: Yet he had long possessed talent and ability; in assisting government he often corrected and benefited affairs; he loved literature and treated scholars with ritual respect—his reputation in the age was very weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was genuinely capable; in governing he often set things right, loved letters, and honored scholars, and the esteem in which the age held him was immense.

sentences.zh: 侍中、領軍將軍元義在門下，兼總禁兵，恃寵驕恣，志欲無極。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant and Commander of the Guards Yuan Yi was at the Chancellery gate, also holding overall command of the forbidden troops; relying on favor he was arrogant and unrestrained, his aims without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant and Commander of the Guards Yuan Yi held the Chancellery gate and controlled the palace troops; swollen with favor, he grew arrogant and boundless in ambition.

sentences.zh: 懌每裁之以法，義由是怨之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qinghe each time restrained him by law; Yuan Yi for this reason resented him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qinghe repeatedly checked him by law, and Yuan Yi came to hate him for it.

sentences.zh: 衛將軍、儀同三司劉騰，權傾內外，吏部希騰意，奏用騰弟為郡，人資乖越。

translations.literal: Liu Teng, General of the Guard and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, tilted power within and without; the Ministry of Personnel curried Teng's intent and memorialized appointing Teng's younger brother to a commandery—the man's qualifications wildly exceeded his rank.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Teng, General of the Guard with honors equal to the Three Dukes, dominated court and capital; the Ministry of Personnel, eager to please him, proposed his younger brother for a prefecture though the man's qualifications were grossly inadequate.

sentences.zh: 懌抑而不奏，騰亦怨之。

translations.literal: The prince suppressed it and would not memorialize; Teng also resented him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince blocked the appointment and refused to memorialize it, and Liu Teng resented him as well.

sentences.zh: 龍驤府長史宋維，弁之子也，懌薦為通直郎，浮薄無行。

translations.literal: Song Wei, chief clerk of the Dragon Prowess Office, was the son of Bian; the prince recommended him as Attendant for Direct Communication—frivolous and without conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Song Wei, chief clerk of the Dragon Prowess Office and son of Bian, was recommended by the prince as Attendant for Direct Communication; he was shallow and dissolute.

sentences.zh: 義許維以富貴，使告司染都尉韓文殊父子謀作亂立懌。

translations.literal: Yuan Yi promised Wei wealth and rank and had him report that Director of the Dye Office Han Wenshu and his son plotted rebellion to set up the Prince of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi promised Song Wei wealth and rank and had him accuse Han Wenshu, Director of the Dye Office, and his son of plotting rebellion to install the Prince of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 懌坐禁止，按驗，無反狀，得釋，維當反坐；

translations.literal: The prince was detained and investigated; no sign of rebellion was found; he was released; Wei should have been punished in turn;
translations.idiomatic: The prince was detained and investigated, but no evidence of treason appeared and he was released; Song Wei should have been punished in turn;

sentences.zh: 義言於太后曰：「今誅維，後有真反者，人莫敢告。」

translations.literal: Yuan Yi said to the Empress Dowager: "If we execute Wei now, when there is a true rebel later, no one will dare report."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi told the Empress Dowager: "Execute Wei now, and when a real rebel appears later no one will dare speak."

sentences.zh: 乃黜維為昌平郡守。

translations.literal: He was thereupon demoted to Administrator of Changping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was merely demoted to Administrator of Changping.

sentences.zh: 義恐懌終為己害，乃與劉騰密謀，使主食中黃門胡定自列云：「懌貨定使毒魏主，若己得為帝，許定以富貴。」

translations.literal: Yuan Yi feared that the Prince of Qinghe would in the end become his harm; he then secretly plotted with Liu Teng and had the chief food-server, Yellow Gate Attendant Hu Ding, confess of himself, saying: "The prince bribed Ding to poison the Wei ruler; if he himself obtained the throne, he promised Ding wealth and rank."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi feared the prince would destroy him in the end; he and Liu Teng plotted in secret and had Hu Ding, a Yellow Gate Attendant who served the emperor's meals, confess voluntarily that the prince had bribed him to poison the Northern Wei emperor and promised him riches if he himself became emperor."

sentences.zh: 帝時年十一，信之。

translations.literal: The emperor was then eleven years old and believed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was eleven years old and believed them.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙子，太后在嘉福殿，未御前殿，義奉帝御顯陽殿，騰閉永巷門，太后不得出。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingzi, the Empress Dowager was in Jiafu Hall and had not yet attended the front hall; Yuan Yi escorted the emperor to Xianyang Hall; Teng closed the Gate of the Long Lane—the Empress Dowager could not go out.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingzi, the Empress Dowager was in Jiafu Hall and had not yet gone to the front hall; Yuan Yi escorted the emperor to Xianyang Hall while Liu Teng shut the Long Lane gate so the Empress Dowager could not leave.

sentences.zh: 懌入，遇義於含章殿後，義厲聲不聽懌入，懌曰：「汝欲反邪！」

translations.literal: The prince entered; he met Yuan Yi behind Hanzhang Hall; Yuan Yi in a harsh voice would not let the prince enter; the prince said: "Do you wish to rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: The prince entered and met Yuan Yi behind Hanzhang Hall; Yuan Yi shouted and barred his way. The prince cried: "Do you mean to rebel?"

sentences.zh: 義曰：「義不反，正欲縛反者耳！」

translations.literal: Yi said: "Yi does not rebel—I mean only to bind the rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi answered: "Yi does not rebel—I am here to seize the rebel!"

sentences.zh: 命宗士及直齋執懌衣袂，將入含章東省，使人防守之。

translations.literal: He ordered court gentlemen and direct guards to seize the prince's sleeves and collar and take him into the eastern office of Hanzhang, setting men to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered court gentlemen and palace guards to seize the prince by the sleeves and take him into the eastern wing of Hanzhang Hall under guard.

sentences.zh: 騰稱詔集公卿議，論懌大逆。

translations.literal: Teng, in the name of an edict, assembled the high ministers to deliberate, charging the prince with great treason.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Teng, claiming an imperial order, assembled the chief ministers to judge the prince guilty of high treason.

sentences.zh: 眾鹹畏義，無敢異者，唯僕射新泰文貞公游肇抗言以為不可，終不下署。

translations.literal: The multitude all feared Yuan Yi; none dared differ; only Vice Director You Zhao, Duke Wenzhen of Xintai, spoke against it holding it impossible, and in the end would not sign below.
translations.idiomatic: All feared Yuan Yi and none dared dissent; only Vice Director You Zhao, Duke Wenzhen of Xintai, spoke out that it could not be done and refused to sign.

sentences.zh: 義、騰持公卿議入奏，俄而得可，夜中殺懌。

translations.literal: Yuan Yi and Teng took the ministers' deliberation in to memorialize; soon approval was obtained; in the middle of the night they killed the prince.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi and Liu Teng submitted the ministers' decision for approval; consent came at once, and in the dead of night they killed the Prince of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 於是詐為太后詔，自稱有疾，還政於帝。

translations.literal: Thereupon they forged an edict in the Empress Dowager's name, declaring herself ill and returning government to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: They then forged an edict in the Empress Dowager's name, claiming she was ill and returning rule to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 幽太后於北宮宣光殿，宮門晝夜長閉，內外斷絕，騰自執管鑰，帝亦不得省見，裁聽傳食而巳。

translations.literal: They confined the Empress Dowager in Xuanguang Hall of the Northern Palace; the palace gates were shut day and night; inside and outside were cut off; Teng himself held the keys; the emperor also could not visit and see her—only food passed in was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: They imprisoned the Empress Dowager in Xuanguang Hall of the Northern Palace; the gates stayed shut day and night and all contact was severed; Liu Teng kept the keys himself, and even the emperor could not see her—only meals were passed in.

sentences.zh: 太后服膳俱廢，不免饑寒，乃歎曰：「養虎得噬，我之謂矣！」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager's clothing and meals were both abolished; she could not escape hunger and cold; she sighed and said: "Raise a tiger and it devours you—so it is said of me!"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager went without proper food and clothing and suffered hunger and cold; she sighed: "Feed a tiger and it devours you—that is me!"

sentences.zh: 又使中常侍酒泉賈粲侍帝書，密令防察動止。

translations.literal: They also had Palace Attendant Jia Can of Jiuquan attend the emperor's studies and secretly ordered him to watch and report his movements.
translations.idiomatic: They also set Palace Attendant Jia Can of Jiuquan to attend the emperor's studies and secretly watch his every move.

sentences.zh: 叉遂與太師高陽王雍等同輔政，帝謂義為姨父。

translations.literal: Yuan Yi then joined Grand Preceptor Prince Yong of Gaoyang and others in assisting government; the emperor called Yuan Yi maternal uncle by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi then joined Grand Preceptor Prince Yong of Gaoyang and others in governing; the emperor called him Uncle by marriage.

sentences.zh: 義與騰表裡擅權，義為外御，騰為內防，常直禁省，共裁刑賞，政無鉅細，決於二人，威振內外，百僚重跡。

translations.literal: Yuan Yi and Teng, inside and outside, monopolized power—Yuan Yi as outer defense, Teng as inner guard; they constantly attended the forbidden offices, together deciding punishments and rewards; in government nothing great or small was not decided by the two men; their awe shook within and without; the hundred officials walked with doubled steps.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi and Liu Teng wielded power in concert—Yi outward, Teng inward—always on duty in the palace, deciding punishments and rewards together; nothing great or small was settled without them; their authority shook court and capital, and officials went in fear with shortened steps.

sentences.zh: 朝野聞懌死，無不喪氣，胡夷為之剺面者數百人。

translations.literal: Court and countryside, hearing of the prince's death, were without exception dispirited; several hundred men of Hu and Yi peoples cut their faces for him.
translations.idiomatic: When court and country heard that the prince was dead, spirits sank everywhere; several hundred men of the northern peoples gashed their faces in mourning.

sentences.zh: 游肇憤邑而卒。

translations.literal: You Zhao died of indignant distress.
translations.idiomatic: You Zhao died of grief and rage.

sentences.zh: 己卯，江、淮、海並溢。

translations.literal: On jimao, the Yangzi, Huai, and sea all overflowed together.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao the Yangzi, Huai, and coastal waters flooded together.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，魏主加元服，大赦，改元正光。

translations.literal: On xinmao, the Wei ruler added the cap of manhood, proclaimed a great amnesty, and changed the era name to Zhengguang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao the Northern Wei emperor came of age, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Zhengguang.

sentences.zh: 魏相州刺史中山文莊王熙，英之子也，與弟給事黃門侍郎略、司徒祭酒纂，皆為清河王懌所厚，聞懌死，起兵於鄴，上表欲誅元義、劉騰，纂亡奔鄴。

translations.literal: Yuan Xi, Prince Wenshuang of Zhongshan and Governor of Xiangzhou of Wei, son of Ying, with his younger brothers Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Lue and Libationer of the Minister of Education Zuan—all were deeply favored by the Prince of Qinghe—hearing of the prince's death, raised troops at Ye and memorialized wishing to execute Yuan Yi and Liu Teng; Zuan fled and ran to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xi, Governor of Xiangzhou and Prince Wenshuang of Zhongshan, son of Ying, together with his brothers Lue, Attendant of the Yellow Gate, and Zuan, Libationer of the Minister of Education—all favorites of the murdered Prince of Qinghe—rose at Ye on hearing of the death and memorialized calling for the execution of Yuan Yi and Liu Teng; Zuan fled to join him at Ye.

sentences.zh: 後十日，長史柳元章等帥城人鼓噪而入，殺其左右，執熙、纂並諸子置於高樓。

translations.literal: Ten days later, Chief Clerk Liu Yuanzhang and others led the city people, clamoring as they entered, killed his attendants, seized Xi and Zuan together with their sons, and placed them on a high tower.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later Chief Clerk Liu Yuanzhang and others led townsfolk storming in with a roar, killed his guards, seized Xi and Zuan with their sons, and held them on a high tower.

sentences.zh: 八月，甲寅，元義遣尚書左丞盧同就斬熙於鄴御，並其子弟。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on jiayin, Yuan Yi sent Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Lu Tong to go and behead Xi at Ye in person, together with his sons and younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiayin, Yuan Yi sent Left Assistant Director Lu Tong to Ye to execute Xi on the spot, together with his sons and brothers.

sentences.zh: 熙好文學，有風儀，名士多與之遊。

translations.literal: Xi loved literature and had fine bearing; eminent men often associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi loved letters and bore himself with grace; many eminent men were his companions.

sentences.zh: 將死，與故知書曰：「吾與弟並蒙皇太后知遇，兄據大州，弟則入侍，殷勤言色，恩同慈母。

translations.literal: About to die, he wrote to old acquaintances, saying: "My brother and I both received the Empress Dowager's knowing favor—elder brother holding a great province, younger brother entering attendance—her earnest words and countenance, her grace like a loving mother.
translations.idiomatic: Facing death, he wrote to old friends: "My brother and I were both favored by the Empress Dowager—he ruling a great province, I serving at court—her kindness in word and face was the kindness of a mother.

sentences.zh: 今皇太后見廢北宮，太傅清河王橫受屠酷，主上幼年，獨在前殿。

translations.literal: Now the Empress Dowager is deposed in the Northern Palace; the Grand Tutor, Prince of Qinghe, suffered slaughter and cruelty in vain; the ruler is young and alone in the front hall.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Empress Dowager is imprisoned in the Northern Palace, the Grand Tutor Prince of Qinghe has been butchered, and the emperor is a child left alone in the front hall.

sentences.zh: 君親如此，無以自安，故帥兵民欲建大義於天下。

translations.literal: Sovereign and parent in such a state—I have no means to be at peace; therefore I lead soldiers and people wishing to establish great righteousness in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: With sovereign and parent both in such straits I could not rest; I therefore took up arms to set righteousness right in the realm.

sentences.zh: 但智力淺短，旋見囚執，上慚朝廷，下愧相知。

translations.literal: But my wisdom and strength were shallow and short; presently I was seized and bound—above I shame the court, below I fail old friends.
translations.idiomatic: But my wit and strength were too slight; I was seized at once—ashamed before the court, failing my friends below.

sentences.zh: 本以名義干心，不得不爾，流腸碎首，復何言哉！

translations.literal: Originally it was righteousness and reputation that moved my heart—I could not do otherwise; bowels streaming, head shattered—what more is there to say!
translations.idiomatic: Duty and honor drove me—I had no choice; my heart is torn and my head is broken—what more can I say!

sentences.zh: 凡百君子，各敬爾儀，為國為射，善勖名節！」

translations.literal: All you gentlemen, each respect your deportment; for the state and for the shoot, diligently exhort your name and integrity!"
translations.idiomatic: All you gentlemen, mind your bearing; serve your state and your households; guard your honor well!"

sentences.zh: 聞者憐之。

translations.literal: Those who heard it pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: All who read it pitied him.

sentences.zh: 熙首至洛陽，親故莫敢視，前驍騎將軍刁整獨收其屍而藏之。

translations.literal: When Xi's head reached Luoyang, kin and friends none dared look; former General of Valiant Cavalry Diao Zheng alone gathered his corpse and hid it.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi's head reached Luoyang, none of his kin and friends dared look upon it; only former General Diao Zheng gathered the body and hid it.

sentences.zh: 整，雍之孫也。

translations.literal: Zheng was the grandson of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Zheng was a grandson of Prince Yong.

sentences.zh: 盧同希義意，窮治熙黨與，鎖濟陰內史楊昱赴鄴，考訊百日，乃得還任。

translations.literal: Lu Tong curried Yuan Yi's intent, exhaustively prosecuted Xi's partisans, chained Yang Yu, Interior Minister of Jiyin, and sent him to Ye; after a hundred days of interrogation he was only then able to return to office.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Tong, eager to please Yuan Yi, hunted Xi's associates to the end, shackled Yang Yu, Interior Minister of Jiyin, and sent him to Ye; only after a hundred days of torture was Yang Yu allowed to resume his post.

sentences.zh: 義以同為黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Yuan Yi made Tong Yellow Gate Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi appointed Lu Tong Yellow Gate Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 元略亡抵故人河內司馬始賓，始賓與略縛荻筏夜渡孟津，詣屯留栗法光家，轉依西河太守刁雙，匿之經年。

translations.literal: Yuan Lue, fleeing, reached his old friend Sima Shibin of Henei; Shibin and Lue bound a reed raft and crossed the Meng ford by night, went to the home of Li Faguang of Tunliu, then turned to rely on Diao Shuang, Governor of Xihe, who hid him for more than a year.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Lue fled to his old friend Sima Shibin of Henei; Shibin and Lue lashed a reed raft and crossed the Meng Ford by night, stopped at the house of Li Faguang of Tunliu, then took refuge with Diao Shuang, Governor of Xihe, who hid him for more than a year.

sentences.zh: 時購略甚急，略懼，求送出境，雙曰：「會有一死，所難遇者為知己死耳，願不以為慮。」

translations.literal: At the time the hunt for Lue was very urgent; Lue was afraid and asked to be sent beyond the border; Shuang said: "One will meet death in any case—the hard thing to encounter is dying for one who knows you; I hope you will not take this as a worry."
translations.idiomatic: The search for Lue was fierce; afraid, he asked to be sent abroad. Shuang said: "We all must die once—the rare thing is to die for a friend; do not trouble yourself on that account."

sentences.zh: 略固求南奔，雙乃使從子昌送略渡江，遂來奔，上封略為中山王。

translations.literal: Lue firmly asked to flee south; Shuang then had his nephew's son Chang escort Lue across the river; he thereupon came to defect, and the emperor enfeoffed Lue as Prince of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Lue insisted on fleeing south; Shuang had his nephew Chang escort him across the Yangzi, and Lue came to Liang, where the emperor enfeoffed him as Prince of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 雙，雍之族孫也。

translations.literal: Shuang was a collateral descendant of Yong in the clan.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Shuang was a collateral descendant of Prince Yong's line.

sentences.zh: 義誣刁整送略，並其子弟收系之，御史王基等力為辨雪，乃得免。

translations.literal: Yuan Yi falsely accused Diao Zheng of escorting Lue and seized him together with his sons and younger brothers; Censor Wang Ji and others strenuously argued his innocence, and he was then spared.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi accused Diao Zheng of helping Lue escape and arrested him with his sons and brothers; Censor Wang Ji and others argued strenuously for his innocence, and he was released.

sentences.zh: 甲子，侍中、車騎將軍永昌嚴侯韋睿卒。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Palace Attendant and General of Chariots and Cavalry Wei Rui, Marquis Yan of Yongchang, died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Palace Attendant and General of Chariots and Cavalry Wei Rui, Marquis Yan of Yongchang, died.

sentences.zh: 時上方崇釋氏，士民無不從風而靡，獨睿自以位居大臣，不欲與俗俯仰，所行略如平日。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor above was exalting the Shakya clan; scholars and commoners none failed to follow the wind and bend; only Rui, considering himself to stand among great ministers, did not wish to bow with the vulgar—his conduct was much as on ordinary days.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then exalting Buddhism and everyone bent with the fashion; only Wei Rui, holding himself a great minister, refused to bob with the crowd and lived much as he always had.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊戌，魏以高陽王雍為丞相，總攝內外，與元義同決庶務。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on wuxu, Wei made Prince Yong of Gaoyang Chancellor, holding overall charge within and without, deciding common affairs together with Yuan Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on wuxu, Northern Wei made Prince Yong of Gaoyang Chancellor with authority over all affairs, sharing decisions with Yuan Yi.

sentences.zh: 初，柔然佗汗可汗納伏名敦之妻候呂陵氏，生伏跋可汁及阿那瑰等六子。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Rouran khan Tuohen of the Tuohan line took as wife Houlü of the Hou clan, wife of Nafuming Dun, and bore Fuba kehan and Anagui among six sons.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Rouran khan Tuohen of the Tuohan line had married Houlü of the Hou clan, widow of Nafuming Dun, and she bore Fuba Khan, Anagui, and four other sons.

sentences.zh: 伏跋既立，忽亡其幼子祖惠，求募不能得。

translations.literal: After Fuba was established, suddenly his young son Zuhui was lost; search and reward could not obtain him.
translations.idiomatic: After Fuba took the throne, his young son Zuhui vanished suddenly; searches and rewards failed to find him.

sentences.zh: 有巫地萬言：「祖惠今在天上，我能呼之。」

translations.literal: A shamaness, Diwan, said: "Zuhui is now in Heaven; I can call him."
translations.idiomatic: A shamaness named Diwan said: "Zuhui is in Heaven now, and I can summon him."

sentences.zh: 乃於大澤中施帳幄，祀天神。

translations.literal: She then set up tents and curtains in the great marsh and sacrificed to the Heavenly God.
translations.idiomatic: She pitched tents in the great marsh and sacrificed to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 祖惠忽在帳中，自雲恆在天上。

translations.literal: Zuhui suddenly appeared in the tent and himself said he had always been in Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Zuhui suddenly appeared inside the tent and said he had always been in Heaven.

sentences.zh: 伏跋大喜，號地萬為聖女，納為可賀敦。

translations.literal: Fuba was greatly pleased, titled Diwan Sacred Woman, and took her as kehudun.
translations.idiomatic: Fuba rejoiced, titled Diwan Sacred Woman, and made her his kehudun.

sentences.zh: 地萬既挾左道，復有姿色，伏跋敬而愛之，信用其言，干亂國政。

translations.literal: Diwan, having seized heterodox ways and also possessing beauty, Fuba revered and loved her, trusted and used her words, and threw state affairs into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Diwan wielded sorcery and was beautiful besides; Fuba revered and loved her, believed whatever she said, and threw the realm into disorder.

sentences.zh: 如是積歲，祖惠浸長，語其母曰：「我常在地萬家，未嘗上天。

translations.literal: Thus for accumulated years; Zuhui gradually grew; he told his mother: "I was always at Diwan's house—I never went to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Years passed and Zuhui grew up; he told his mother: "I was always at Diwan's house—I never went to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 『上天』者，地萬教我也。」

translations.literal: What is called 'going to Heaven'—Diwan taught me that."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven' was only what Diwan taught me to say."

sentences.zh: 其母具以狀告伏跋，伏跋曰：「地萬能前知未然，勿為讒也！」

translations.literal: His mother reported the entire situation to Fuba. Fuba said: "Diwan can know beforehand what has not yet occurred—do not take it as slander!"
translations.idiomatic: His mother told Fuba everything that had happened. Fuba said: "Diwan can foresee what has not yet come to pass—do not heed slander!"

sentences.zh: 既而地萬懼，譖祖惠於伏跋而殺之。

translations.literal: Before long Diwan grew afraid; she slandered Zuhui to Fuba, and he had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Diwan grew afraid; she denounced Zuhui to Fuba, and Fuba had him killed.

sentences.zh: 候呂陵氏遣其大臣具列等絞殺地萬；

translations.literal: Houlü dispatched her grand ministers Julie and others to strangle Diwan;
translations.idiomatic: Houlü sent her chief ministers, including Julie, to strangle Diwan;

sentences.zh: 伏跋怒，欲誅具列等。

translations.literal: Fuba was enraged and wished to execute Julie and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Fuba was furious and wanted to put Julie and his colleagues to death.

sentences.zh: 會阿至羅入寇，伏跋擊之，兵敗而還。

translations.literal: Just then Aziluo raided; Fuba struck him, was defeated in battle, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment Aziluo invaded; Fuba attacked him, was routed, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 候呂陵氏與大臣共殺伏跋，立其弟阿那瑰為可汗。

translations.literal: Houlü with the grand ministers jointly killed Fuba and installed his younger brother Anagui as khan.
translations.idiomatic: Houlü and the chief ministers killed Fuba together and set up his younger brother Anagui as khan.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰立十日，其族兄示發帥眾數萬擊之，阿那瑰戰敗，與其弟乙居伐輕騎奔魏。

translations.literal: Anagui had been khan ten days when his clansman elder Shifa led tens of thousands to attack him; Anagui was defeated in battle and, with his younger brother Yijufa, fled to Wei with light cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days after Anagui took the throne, his elder clansman Shifa led tens of thousands against him; Anagui was defeated and fled to Wei with light cavalry alongside his brother Yijufa.

sentences.zh: 示發殺候呂陵氏及阿那瑰二弟。

translations.literal: Shifa killed Houlü and Anagui's two younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Shifa killed Houlü and Anagui's two younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 魏清河王懌死，汝南王悅了無恨元義之意，以桑落酒候之，盡其私佞。

translations.literal: Prince Qinghe Yi of Wei died; Prince Runan Yue harbored not the least resentment toward Yuan Yi and, with mulberry-drop wine, waited on him, exhausting private flattery.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Qinghe Yi of Wei died, Prince Runan Yue showed not a trace of ill will toward Yuan Yi; he attended him with mulberry-drop wine and lavished every sort of private sycophancy.

sentences.zh: 義大喜，冬，十月，乙卯，以悅為侍中、大尉。

translations.literal: Yi was greatly pleased; in winter, the tenth month, on yimao, Yue was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi was delighted; in winter, the tenth month, on yimao, Yue was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 悅就懌子但求懌服玩，不時稱旨，杖但百下，幾死。

translations.literal: Yue went to Prince Yi's son Dan to seek Prince Yi's garments and curios; not pleasing him in a timely way, Dan had him beaten a hundred strokes—he nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: Yue went to Yi's son Yuan Dan to demand Yi's robes and treasures; when he failed to please him promptly, Dan had him beaten a hundred times—he nearly died.

sentences.zh: 柔然可汗阿那瑰將至魏，魏主使司空京兆王繼、侍中崔光等相次迎之，賜勞甚厚。

translations.literal: The Rouran khan Anagui was about to reach Wei; the Wei emperor sent Minister of Works Prince of Jingzhao Ji, Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang, and others in succession to welcome him, with very generous gifts and comfort.
translations.idiomatic: As Rouran khan Anagui was nearing Wei, the Northern Wei emperor sent Minister of Works Prince Ji of Jingzhao, Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang, and others in turn to welcome him with lavish rewards and consolation.

sentences.zh: 魏主引見阿那瑰於顯陽殿，因置宴，置阿那瑰位於親王之下。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor received Anagui at the Hall of Splendid Yang and then held a feast, setting Anagui's seat below that of imperial princes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received Anagui at the Hall of Splendid Yang and held a banquet, placing him below the imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 宴將罷，阿那瑰執啟立於座後，詔引至御座前，阿那瑰再拜言曰：「臣以家難，輕來詣闕，本國臣民，皆已逃散。

translations.literal: As the feast was ending, Anagui held a memorial and stood behind his seat; an edict drew him before the imperial seat. Anagui bowed twice and said: "I, your subject, because of domestic distress came lightly to the court; the people of my state have all fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: When the banquet was nearly over, Anagui stood behind his seat holding a memorial; an edict summoned him before the throne. Anagui bowed twice and said: "Brought low by troubles at home, I came hastily to your court; the people of my country have all fled and scattered.

sentences.zh: 陛下恩隆天地，乞兵送還本國，誅剪叛逆，收集亡散。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's grace is lofty as Heaven and Earth; I beg troops to escort me back to my state, to cut down rebels and gather the lost and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's kindness towers like Heaven and Earth; I beg you to send troops to restore me to my realm, to punish rebels, and to gather those who have fled.

sentences.zh: 臣當統帥遺民，奉事陛下。

translations.literal: I shall lead the surviving people and serve Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I will lead the remnant people and serve Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 言不能盡，別有啟陳。」

translations.literal: Words cannot exhaust it; I have another memorial to present separately."
translations.idiomatic: I cannot say all that is in my heart; I have another memorial to submit separately."

sentences.zh: 仍以啟授中書舍人常景以聞。

translations.literal: He then handed the memorial to Palace Secretary Chang Jing to report.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave the memorial to Palace Secretary Chang Jing to present.

sentences.zh: 景，爽之孫也。

translations.literal: Jing was the grandson of Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Jing was a grandson of Chang Shuang.

sentences.zh: 十一月，己亥，魏立阿那瑰為朔方公、蠕蠕，王，賜以衣服、軺車。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jihai, Wei established Anagui as Duke of Shuofang and king of Rouran, granting him garments and a light carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jihai, Northern Wei made Anagui Duke of Shuofang and king of Rouran, granting him robes and a light carriage.

sentences.zh: 祿恤儀衛，一如親王。

translations.literal: Stipends, comforts, guards and insignia—all like an imperial prince.
translations.idiomatic: Salary, allowances, guards, and insignia matched those of an imperial prince.

sentences.zh: 時魏方強盛，於洛水橋南御道東作四館，道西立四里：有自江南來降者處之金陵館，三年之後賜宅于歸正裡；

translations.literal: At this time Wei was flourishing; south of the Luo Bridge on the east of the imperial road four lodges were built, and on the west of the road four wards were established: those who surrendered from south of the Yangtze were lodged in Jinling Lodge; three years later they were granted residences in Guizheng Ward;
translations.idiomatic: Wei was then at its height; south of the Luo Bridge, four guesthouses were built east of the imperial avenue and four wards west of it: defectors from south of the Yangtze stayed in Jinling Lodge, and after three years received homes in Guizheng Ward;

sentences.zh: 自北夷降者處燕然館，賜宅于歸德裡；

translations.literal: those who surrendered from northern barbarians were lodged in Yanran Lodge and granted residences in Guide Ward;
translations.idiomatic: northern barbarians who surrendered were housed in Yanran Lodge and given homes in Guide Ward;

sentences.zh: 自東夷降者處扶桑館，賜宅於慕化裡；

translations.literal: those from eastern barbarians were lodged in Fusang Lodge and granted residences in Muhua Ward;
translations.idiomatic: eastern barbarians were lodged in Fusang Lodge and settled in Muhua Ward;

sentences.zh: 自西夷降者處崦嵫館，賜宅於慕義裡。

translations.literal: those from western barbarians were lodged in Yanzi Lodge and granted residences in Muyi Ward.
translations.idiomatic: western barbarians were lodged in Yanzi Lodge and settled in Muyi Ward.

sentences.zh: 及阿那瑰入朝，以燕然館處之。

translations.literal: When Anagui came to court, he was lodged in Yanran Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: When Anagui came to court, he was placed in Yanran Lodge.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰屢求返國，朝議異同不決，阿那瑰以金百斤賂元義，遂聽北歸。

translations.literal: Anagui repeatedly sought to return to his state; court debate was divided and no decision was made. Anagui bribed Yuan Yi with a hundred catties of gold, and he was then permitted to return north.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui repeatedly asked to go home; court opinion was split and no decision could be reached until he bribed Yuan Yi with a hundred catties of gold and was at last allowed to return north.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬子，魏敕懷朔都督簡銳騎二千護送阿那瑰達境首，觀機招納。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on renzi, Wei ordered the Huai-shuo commander to pick two thousand elite cavalry to escort Anagui to the border head, observing circumstances to win people over.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on renzi, Wei ordered the Huai-shuo commander to select two thousand picked horsemen to escort Anagui to the frontier and win adherents as opportunity allowed.

sentences.zh: 若彼迎候，宜賜繒帛車馬禮餞而返；

translations.literal: If they welcome him, they should bestow silk, horses and carriages, farewell gifts and return;
translations.idiomatic: If the Rouran receive him, they should be given silk, horses, carriages, and parting gifts and sent back;

sentences.zh: 如不容受，聽還闕庭。
