translations.literal: if they do not receive him, he is permitted to return to the palace court.
translations.idiomatic: if they refuse him, he may return to the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 其行裝資遣，付尚書量給。

translations.literal: His traveling gear and travel expenses were entrusted to the Masters of Writing to measure out and supply.
translations.idiomatic: His baggage and travel funds were left to the Masters of Writing to calculate and issue.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，魏以京光王繼為司徒。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Wei made Prince of Jingzhao Ji Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Northern Wei appointed Prince Ji of Jingzhao Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 魏遺使者劉善明來聘，始復通好。

translations.literal: Wei sent the envoy Liu Shanming on a friendly mission; good relations were resumed.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei sent the envoy Liu Shanming on a friendly mission, and cordial relations were restored.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝五普通二年（

translations.literal: The Martial Emperor Gaozu, second year of Putong (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang, second year of Putong (

sentences.zh: 辛丑，公元五二一年）

translations.literal: xinchou, corresponding to the year 521 CE)
translations.idiomatic: xinchou, corresponding to 521 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛巳，上祀南郊。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on xinsi, the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on xinsi, the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 置孤獨園於建康，以收養窮民。

translations.literal: A Solitary Garden was established at Jiankang to take in the destitute.
translations.idiomatic: A Solitary Garden was established at Jiankang to shelter the poor.

sentences.zh: 戊子，大赦。

translations.literal: On wuzi, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 魏南秦州氐反。

translations.literal: The Di of Southern Qinzhou in Wei rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The Di of Southern Qin in Northern Wei rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 魏發近郡兵萬五千人，使懷朔鎮將楊鈞將之，送柔然可汗阿那瑰返國。

translations.literal: Wei mobilized fifteen thousand troops from nearby commanderies, had the Huai-shuo garrison general Yang Jun lead them, and escorted the Rouran khan Anagui back to his state.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei raised fifteen thousand men from neighboring commanderies, put Huai-shuo garrison commander Yang Jun in command, and sent Rouran khan Anagui home.

sentences.zh: 尚書右丞張普惠上疏，以為：「蠕蠕久為邊患，今茲天降喪亂，荼毒其心，蓋欲使之知有道之可樂，革面稽首以奉大魏也。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Zhang Puhui submitted a memorial, stating: "Rouran has long been a border scourge; now Heaven has sent down disorder to afflict their hearts—surely this is meant to make them know the joy of the Way, turn their faces and bow to serve great Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Puhui, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, memorialized: "The Rouran have long plagued our borders; now Heaven has visited ruin upon them and poisoned their hearts—surely so they may learn the blessings of the Way, change their ways, and bow to serve Great Wei.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜安民恭己，以悅服其心。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should settle the people and restrain yourself, to please and win their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should quiet the people and govern with restraint, so as to win their hearts.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰束身歸命，撫之可也；

translations.literal: Anagui has bound himself and submitted; comforting him will suffice;
translations.idiomatic: Anagui has come in person to submit; it is enough to comfort him;

sentences.zh: 乃更先自勞擾，興師郊甸之內，投諸荒裔之外，救累世之勍敵，資天亡之丑虜。

translations.literal: yet you would first trouble yourselves, raise troops within the suburban domains, and cast them beyond the wild borderlands—rescuing a fierce foe of many generations and supplying a ugly captive Heaven is destroying.
translations.idiomatic: yet you would first wear yourselves out, raise armies within the capital domains, and send them to the outer wastes—rescuing a foe fierce for generations and arming a detestable remnant Heaven itself is wiping out.

sentences.zh: 臣愚，未見其可也。

translations.literal: Your subject is foolish and does not see how this can be approved.
translations.idiomatic: This humble subject cannot see how that can be right.

sentences.zh: 此乃邊將貪竊一時之功，不思兵為凶器，王者不得已而用之。

translations.literal: This is border generals greedy to steal momentary merit, not reflecting that arms are an ill omen and kings use them only when they have no choice.
translations.idiomatic: This is frontier commanders grasping for a moment's glory, forgetting that war is an ill omen and that kings employ it only when they must.

sentences.zh: 況今旱暵方甚，聖慈降膳，乃以萬五千人使楊鈞為將，而欲定蠕蠕干時而動，其可濟乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, drought is now severe and Your Sagely kindness has reduced meals—yet fifteen thousand men are placed under Yang Jun as general to settle Rouran while they stir at an inopportune time; how can this succeed!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover drought now grips the land and Your Majesty has cut his own meals—yet fifteen thousand men under Yang Jun are sent to settle the Rouran while they move at the wrong moment; how can that succeed?

sentences.zh: 脫有顛覆之變，楊鈞之肉，其足食乎！

translations.literal: If there should be a disastrous reversal, would Yang Jun's flesh be enough to eat!
translations.idiomatic: If disaster strikes, will there even be enough of Yang Jun's flesh to go around!

sentences.zh: 宰輔專好小名，不圖安危大計，此微臣所以寒心者也。

translations.literal: The chief ministers devote themselves only to petty reputation and do not plan for the great matter of safety and peril—this is why your lowly subject is chilled at heart.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers care only for petty fame and plot nothing for the realm's safety—this is what fills your humble servant with dread.

sentences.zh: 且阿那瑰之不還，負何信義，臣賤不及議，文書所過，不敢不陳。」

translations.literal: Moreover, if Anagui does not return, what faith and righteousness would be violated? Your subject is too low to join in deliberation; wherever documents pass, he dares not fail to state it."
translations.idiomatic: And if Anagui does not return, what bond of trust would be broken? I am too low to debate policy, but wherever papers cross my desk I dare not stay silent."

sentences.zh: 弗聽。

translations.literal: It was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not listen.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰辭於西堂，詔賜以軍器、衣被、雜采、糧畜，事事優厚，命侍中崔光等勞遣於外郭。

translations.literal: Anagui took leave at the Western Hall; an edict granted him military gear, clothing, bedding, assorted silks, grain and livestock—each item generously—and ordered Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang and others to see him off at the outer city.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui took his leave in the Western Hall; an edict gave him arms, clothing, bedding, silks, grain, and livestock in lavish measure, and ordered Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang and others to escort him beyond the outer wall.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰之南奔也，其從父兄婆羅門帥眾數萬入討示發，破之，示發奔地豆乾，地豆乾殺之，國人推婆羅門為彌偶可社句可汗。

translations.literal: When Anagui fled south, his father's younger brother by clan Borumen led tens of thousands to campaign against Shifa, defeated him; Shifa fled to Didougan, Didougan killed him, and the people raised Borumen as khan Miou ke she ju.
translations.idiomatic: When Anagui fled south, his uncle Borumen led tens of thousands against Shifa, defeated him, and Shifa fled to Didougan, who killed him; the people then set up Borumen as khan Miou ke she ju.

sentences.zh: 楊鈞表稱：「柔然已立君長，恐未肯以殺兄之人郊迎其弟。

translations.literal: Yang Jun memorialized, stating: "Rouran have already established a lord; I fear they will not be willing to welcome at the border a man who killed his brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun reported: "The Rouran already have a ruler; they are unlikely to greet at the frontier a brother of the man who killed their khan.

sentences.zh: 輕往虛返，徒損國威。

translations.literal: To go lightly and return empty will only harm the state's prestige.
translations.idiomatic: A futile journey would only damage imperial prestige.

sentences.zh: 自非廣加兵眾，無以送其入北。」

translations.literal: Unless troops are greatly increased, there is no way to send him into the north."
translations.idiomatic: Unless we greatly increase the army, we cannot escort him home."

sentences.zh: 二月，魏人使舊嘗奉使柔然者牒雲具仁往諭婆羅門，使迎阿那瑰。

translations.literal: In the second month, the Wei sent Dieyun Juren, who had formerly served as envoy to Rouran, to instruct Borumen to welcome Anagui.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Northern Wei sent Dieyun Juren, who had once been envoy to the Rouran, to urge Borumen to receive Anagui.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，上祀明堂。

translations.literal: On xinchou, the emperor sacrificed at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, the emperor sacrificed at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，魏使假撫軍將軍邴虯討南秦叛氐。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Wei sent Acting General Who Pacifies the Army Bing Qiu to campaign against the rebellious Di of Southern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Northern Wei sent Acting General Who Pacifies the Army Bing Qiu to suppress the Di rebels of Southern Qin.

sentences.zh: 魏元義、劉騰之幽胡太后也，右衛將軍奚康生預其謀，義以康生為撫軍大將軍、河南尹，仍使之領左右。

translations.literal: When Yuan Yi and Liu Teng imprisoned Empress Dowager Hu, Right Guard General Xi Kangsheng took part in the plot; Yi made Kangsheng General Who Pacifies the Army, Intendant of Henan, and still had him command the Left and Right.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Yi and Liu Teng imprisoned Empress Dowager Hu, Right Guard General Xi Kangsheng had shared in the plot; Yi made him General Who Pacifies the Army and Intendant of Henan and kept him in charge of the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 康生子難當娶侍中、左衛將軍侯剛女，剛子，義之妹夫也，義以康生通姻，深相委託，三人率多俱宿禁中，時或迭出，以難當為千牛備身。

translations.literal: Kangsheng's son Nandang married the daughter of Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Guard General Hou Gang; Gang's son was Yi's sister's husband. Yi, because Kangsheng was connected by marriage, deeply entrusted him; the three men mostly lodged together in the forbidden precinct, sometimes taking turns to go out, and Nandang was made a thousand-ox bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng's son Nandang married the daughter of Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Guard General Hou Gang, whose son was married to Yi's sister. Trusting the marriage tie, Yi relied heavily on Kangsheng; the three often slept together inside the palace, going out by turns, and Nandang was made a thousand-ox bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 康生性粗武，言氣高下，義稍憚之，見於顏色，康生亦微懼不安。

translations.literal: Kangsheng's nature was rough and martial; his speech and bearing rose and fell; Yi came slightly to fear him, and this showed in his face; Kangsheng also grew slightly fearful and uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng was coarse and warlike, his tone imperious; Yi began to fear him, and it showed; Kangsheng in turn grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 甲午，魏主朝太后於西林園，文武侍坐，酒酣迭舞，康生乃為力士舞，及折旋之際，每顧視太后，舉手、蹈足、瞋目、頷首，為執殺之勢，太后解其意而不敢言。

translations.literal: On jiawu, the Wei emperor attended on the empress dowager at Western Grove Garden; civil and military officials sat in attendance; when the wine was deep they danced in turn. Kangsheng then performed a strongman's dance, and at the turns of the whirl each time he looked toward the empress dowager, raising hands, stamping feet, glaring, and nodding—making the posture of seizing and killing; the empress dowager understood his meaning but did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, the Northern Wei emperor visited the empress dowager at Western Grove Garden; civil and military officials attended; as wine deepened they danced in turn. Kangsheng performed a warrior dance, and at each spin he glanced at the empress dowager, lifting his hands, stamping, glaring, and nodding as if to seize and kill her; she understood but dared not speak.

sentences.zh: 日暮，太后欲攜帝宿宣光殿，侯剛曰：「至尊已朝訖，嬪御在南，何必留宿！」

translations.literal: At dusk the empress dowager wished to take the emperor to lodge in Xuanguang Hall; Hou Gang said: "The Son of Heaven has already finished his audience; the consorts are in the south—why must you stay the night!"
translations.idiomatic: At dusk the empress dowager wanted to keep the emperor overnight in Xuanguang Hall; Hou Gang said: "His Majesty has already concluded his audience; the consorts are in the south—why stay the night?"

sentences.zh: 康生曰：「至尊陛下之兒，隨陛下將東西，更復訪誰！」

translations.literal: Kangsheng said: "The Son of Heaven is Your Majesty's son; he will follow Your Majesty east or west—whom else would you consult!"
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng said: "The Son of Heaven is Your Majesty's son; wherever you go he goes—whom else need you ask?"

sentences.zh: 群臣莫敢應。

translations.literal: None of the officials dared reply.
translations.idiomatic: No minister dared answer.

sentences.zh: 太后自起授帝臂，下堂而去。

translations.literal: The empress dowager herself rose, took the emperor's arm, and left the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager rose, took the emperor's arm, and left the hall.

sentences.zh: 康生大呼，唱萬歲。

translations.literal: Kangsheng shouted loudly, proclaiming "Long live!"
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng shouted "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 帝前入閤，左右競相排，閤不得閉。

translations.literal: The emperor went forward into the side chamber; attendants scrambled to push one another; the door could not be closed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hurried into the side chamber; attendants shoved one another in the rush and the door would not shut.

sentences.zh: 康生奪難當千牛刀，斫直後元思輔，乃得定。

translations.literal: Kangsheng seized Nandang's thousand-ox sword, hacked the attendant behind Yuan Sifu, and only then was it settled.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng snatched Nandang's thousand-ox blade, struck down attendant Yuan Sifu, and at last restored order.

sentences.zh: 帝既升宣光殿，左右侍臣俱立西階下。

translations.literal: After the emperor had ascended Xuanguang Hall, the attending officials all stood below the western steps.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor reached Xuanguang Hall, the attending officials all stood at the foot of the western stairs.

sentences.zh: 康生乘酒勢將出處分，為義所執，鎖於門下。

translations.literal: Kangsheng, riding the force of wine, was about to go out and give orders; he was seized by Yi and locked in the Gate Office.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, Kangsheng was about to go out and issue commands; Yi seized him and chained him in the Gate Office.

sentences.zh: 光祿勳賈粲紿太后曰：「侍官懷恐不安，陛下宜親安慰。」

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Household Jia Can deceived the empress dowager, saying: "The attendants harbor fear and are uneasy; Your Majesty should go down in person to comfort them."
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Imperial Household Jia Can tricked the empress dowager: "The guards are terrified; Your Majesty should go down yourself to reassure them."

sentences.zh: 太后信之，適下殿，粲即扶帝出東序，前御顯陽殿，閉太后於宣光殿。

translations.literal: The empress dowager believed him; just as she came down from the hall, Can immediately supported the emperor out the eastern passage, advanced to the Hall of Splendid Yang, and shut the empress dowager in Xuanguang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: She believed him; as she stepped down, Can at once led the emperor out the eastern passage to the Hall of Splendid Yang and locked the empress dowager in Xuanguang Hall.

sentences.zh: 至晚，義不出，令侍中、黃門、僕射、尚書等十餘人就康生所訊其事，處康生斬刑、難當絞刑。

translations.literal: By evening Yi did not come out; he ordered more than ten Attendants-in-Ordinary, Yellow Gate officials, Masters of Writing, and others to go to Kangsheng's place to examine the affair; they sentenced Kangsheng to decapitation and Nandang to strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: By nightfall Yi still did not emerge; he sent more than ten chief ministers and secretaries to Kangsheng's cell to investigate, sentencing Kangsheng to beheading and Nandang to strangulation.

sentences.zh: 義與剛並在內，矯詔決之：「康生如奏，難當恕死從流。」

translations.literal: Yi and Gang were both inside; they forged an edict deciding it: "Kangsheng as memorialized; Nandang spared death and exiled."
translations.idiomatic: Yi and Gang were inside together; they forged an edict: "Kangsheng as ruled; Nandang spared and banished."

sentences.zh: 難當哭辭父，康生慷慨不悲，曰：「我不反死，汝何哭也！」

translations.literal: Nandang wept taking leave of his father; Kangsheng was ardent and not sorrowful, saying: "I did not rebel—why do you weep!"
translations.idiomatic: Nandang wept farewell to his father; Kangsheng showed no grief and said: "I did not rebel—why weep?"

sentences.zh: 時已昏暗，有司驅康生赴市，斬之。

translations.literal: It was already dark; the authorities drove Kangsheng to the market and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Night had fallen; the authorities marched Kangsheng to the marketplace and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 尚食典御奚混與康生同執刀入內，亦坐絞。

translations.literal: Chief of Imperial Provisions Xi Hun had entered with Kangsheng holding blades; he was also sentenced to strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: Chief of Imperial Provisions Xi Hun, who had entered with Kangsheng bearing swords, was also condemned to strangulation.

sentences.zh: 難當以侯剛婿，得留百餘日，竟流安州；

translations.literal: Because Nandang was Hou Gang's son-in-law, he was kept more than a hundred days and in the end was exiled to Anzhou;
translations.idiomatic: As Hou Gang's son-in-law, Nandang was held more than a hundred days and finally banished to Anzhou;

sentences.zh: 久之，義使行台盧同就殺之。

translations.literal: after a long time, Yi sent Mobile Corps Lu Tong to go and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: long afterward Yi sent Mobile Corps commissioner Lu Tong to kill him there.

sentences.zh: 以劉騰為司空。

translations.literal: Liu Teng was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Teng was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 八坐、九卿常旦造騰宅，參其顏色，然後赴省府，亦有歷日不能見者。

translations.literal: The Eight Seats and Nine Ministers regularly at dawn visited Teng's house, observed his expression, and only then went to their ministries; some went days without being received.
translations.idiomatic: The Eight Seats and Nine Ministers called at Teng's house each dawn to read his mood before going to office; some waited days without an audience.

sentences.zh: 公私屬請，唯視貨多少。

translations.literal: Public and private petitions looked only at how much goods were offered.
translations.idiomatic: Public and private requests were granted solely according to the bribe.

sentences.zh: 舟車之利，山澤之饒，所在榷固，刻剝六鎮，交通互市，歲入利息以巨萬萬計。

translations.literal: Profit from boats and carts, bounty of mountains and marshes—wherever they were, monopolies were fixed; the Six Garrisons were harshly stripped; he traded at border markets, and yearly interest income was reckoned in the tens of billions.
translations.idiomatic: He monopolized transport and mountain resources alike, squeezed the Six Garrisons, traded at frontier markets, and drew yearly profits reckoned in the tens of billions.

sentences.zh: 逼奪鄰舍以廣其居，遠近苦之。

translations.literal: He seized neighbors' houses to enlarge his residence; near and far suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: He seized neighboring homes to expand his mansion, to the misery of all around.

sentences.zh: 京兆王繼自以父子權位太盛，固請以司徒讓車騎大將軍、儀同三司崔光。

translations.literal: Prince Ji of Jingzhao, considering that father and son held too much power, firmly requested to yield the post of Minister of Works to General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes Cui Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ji of Jingzhao, thinking his family held too much power, firmly asked to yield the Ministry of Works to General of Chariots and Cavalry Cui Guang, Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚子，以繼為太保，侍中如故；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on gengzi, Ji was made Grand Tutor, Attendant-in-Ordinary as before;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on gengzi, Ji was made Grand Tutor while remaining Attendant-in-Ordinary;

sentences.zh: 繼固辭，不許。

translations.literal: Ji firmly declined; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Ji declined again; the court would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以崔光為司徒，侍中、祭酒、著作如故。

translations.literal: On renyin, Cui Guang was made Minister of Works; Attendant-in-Ordinary, Libationer, and Compiler of Writings as before.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Cui Guang was appointed Minister of Works, retaining his posts as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Libationer, and Compiler.

sentences.zh: 魏牒雲具仁至柔然，婆羅門殊驕慢，無遜避心，責具仁禮敬；

translations.literal: When Wei's Dieyun Juren reached Rouran, Borumen was extremely arrogant, with no mind to yield; he reproached Juren for lack of courtesy;
translations.idiomatic: When Dieyun Juren of Northern Wei reached the Rouran, Borumen was insufferably arrogant and showed no deference; he demanded that Juren show respect;

sentences.zh: 具仁不屈，婆羅門乃遣大臣丘升頭等將兵二千，隨具仁迎阿那瑰。

translations.literal: Juren would not bend; Borumen then sent the minister Qiutou and others with two thousand troops to follow Juren in welcoming Anagui.
translations.idiomatic: Juren refused to bow; Borumen then sent the minister Qiutou with two thousand men to accompany Juren in receiving Anagui.

sentences.zh: 五月，具仁還鎮，具道其狀。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Juren returned to the garrison and reported the full situation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Juren returned to the garrison and reported everything.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰懼，不敢進，上表請還洛陽。

translations.literal: Anagui was afraid and did not dare advance; he submitted a memorial asking to return to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui was afraid to advance and memorialized asking to return to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，魏南荊州刺史桓叔興據所部來降。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Huan Shuxing, governor of Southern Jing in Wei, held his commandery and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Northern Wei's governor of Southern Jing, Huan Shuxing, brought his district in surrender.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁卯，義州刺史文僧明、邊城太守田守德擁所部降魏，皆蠻酋也。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on dingmao, Yi Prefecture governor Wen Sengming and Biancheng prefect Tian Shoude led their districts to surrender to Wei; all were Man chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on dingmao, Yi Prefecture governor Wen Sengming and Biancheng prefect Tian Shoude led their districts to defect to Northern Wei; both were Man chieftains.

sentences.zh: 魏以僧明為西豫州刺史，守德為義州刺史。

translations.literal: Wei made Sengming governor of Western Yuzhou and Shoude governor of Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei made Sengming governor of Western Yuzhou and Shoude governor of Yi.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，琬琰殿火，延燒後宮三千間。

translations.literal: On guimao, Wan Yan Hall caught fire; the blaze spread through three thousand rooms of the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Wan Yan Hall caught fire, and flames spread through three thousand chambers of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丁酉，以大匠卿裴邃為信武將軍，假節，督眾軍討義州，破魏義州刺史封壽於檀公峴，遂圍其城；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on dingyou, Grand Master of Works Pei Sui was made General of Trustworthy Martiality, with provisional credentials, to command the armies campaigning against Yi Prefecture; he defeated Northern Wei's governor of Yi, Feng Shou, at Tan Gong pass and then besieged the city;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on dingyou, Grand Master of Works Pei Sui was made General of Trustworthy Martiality with provisional credentials to lead the armies against Yi Prefecture; he defeated Northern Wei's Yi governor Feng Shou at Tan Gong Ridge and besieged the city;

sentences.zh: 壽請降，復取義州。

translations.literal: Shou asked to surrender, and they recovered Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shou sought to surrender, and Yi Prefecture was taken back.

sentences.zh: 魏以尚書左丞張普惠為行台，將兵救之，不及。

translations.literal: Wei appointed Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Zhang Puhui as mobile corps commissioner, led troops to rescue him, but did not arrive in time.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Zhang Puhui mobile corps commissioner and sent troops to relieve the siege, but they arrived too late.

sentences.zh: 以裴邃為豫州刺史，鎮合肥。

translations.literal: Pei Sui was made governor of Yuzhou and garrisoned Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Sui was appointed governor of Yuzhou and stationed at Hefei.

sentences.zh: 邃欲襲壽陽，陰結壽陽民李瓜花等為內應。

translations.literal: Sui wished to strike Shouyang and secretly won the Shouyang men Li Guahua and others as inside collaborators.
translations.idiomatic: Sui planned a surprise attack on Shouyang and secretly enlisted Shouyang locals Li Guahua and others as inside agents.

sentences.zh: 邃已勒兵為期日，恐魏覺之，先移魏揚州云：「魏始於馬頭置戍，如聞復欲修白捺故城，若爾，便相侵逼，此亦須營歐陽，設交境之備。

translations.literal: Sui had already mustered troops for the appointed day, fearing Wei would notice; he first sent a dispatch to Wei's Yangzhou saying: "Wei first placed a garrison at Matou; I hear you again wish to repair the old city of Bainai—if so, you will press upon us; this also requires fortifying Ouyang and establishing border defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Sui had already mustered troops for the appointed day and, fearing Wei would notice, first sent a dispatch to Northern Wei's Yangzhou saying: "You first placed a garrison at Matou; I hear you again mean to repair the old city of Bainai—if so, you will press on us; we too must fortify Ouyang and set border defenses.

sentences.zh: 今板卒已集，唯聽信還。」

translations.literal: Now the carpenters and soldiers are assembled; I await only your reply."
translations.idiomatic: Our carpenters and troops are already assembled; I await only your reply."

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史長孫稚謀於僚佐，皆曰：「此無修白捺之意，宜以實報之。」

translations.literal: Yangzhou governor Zhangsun Zhi consulted his staff; all said: "There is no intention here to repair Bainai; the truth should be reported."
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou governor Zhangsun Zhi consulted his staff, who all said: "There is no plan to repair Bainai; we should report the facts."

sentences.zh: 錄事參軍楊侃曰：「白捺小城，本非形勝；

translations.literal: Recording Secretary Yang Kan said: "Bainai is a small city and was never a strategic strong point;
translations.idiomatic: Recording Secretary Yang Kan said: "Bainai is a small town and was never a strategic position;

sentences.zh: 邃好狡數，今集兵遣移，恐有它意。」

translations.literal: Sui loves crafty stratagems; now he gathers troops and sends dispatches—I fear he has another purpose."
translations.idiomatic: Sui is fond of cunning schemes; he is mustering troops and sending dispatches—I fear he has some other design."

sentences.zh: 稚大寤，曰：「錄事可亟作移報之。」

translations.literal: Zhi greatly awoke to it and said: "Recording Secretary, quickly draft a reply dispatch."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi came fully alert and said: "Recording Secretary, draft a reply at once."

sentences.zh: 侃報移曰：「彼之纂兵，想別有意，何為妄構白捺！

translations.literal: Kan's reply dispatch said: "His gathering of troops surely has another purpose—why falsely invoke Bainai!
translations.idiomatic: Kan's reply said: "His mustering of troops surely has another purpose—why invent this tale of Bainai!

sentences.zh: 他人有心，予忖度之，勿謂秦無人也。」

translations.literal: When another has intent, I measure it in my mind—do not say Qin has no men."
translations.idiomatic: When another has designs, I can read them—do not think Qin has no one who sees through you."

sentences.zh: 邃得移，以為魏人已覺，即散其兵。

translations.literal: Sui received the dispatch, thought the men of Wei had detected him, and at once dispersed his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Sui received the dispatch, believed Wei had detected the plot, and immediately dispersed his troops.

sentences.zh: 瓜花等以失期，遂相告發，伏誅者十餘家。

translations.literal: Guahua and the others, because the deadline was missed, then informed on one another; more than ten households suffered execution.
translations.idiomatic: Guahua and the others, the deadline having been missed, turned on one another; more than ten families were executed.

sentences.zh: 稚，觀之子；

translations.literal: Zhi was the son of Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was the son of Guan.

sentences.zh: 侃，播之子也。

translations.literal: Kan was the son of Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Kan was the son of Bo.

sentences.zh: 初，高車王彌俄突死，其眾悉歸厭噠；

translations.literal: Initially, when the Gaoche king Miyetu died, his followers all went over to the Ephthalites;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Gaoche king Miyetu died, his people all submitted to the Ephthalites;

sentences.zh: 後數年，厭噠遣彌俄突弟伊匐帥餘眾還國。

translations.literal: years later the Ephthalites sent Miyetu's younger brother Yifu to lead the remaining followers back to their state.
translations.idiomatic: some years later the Ephthalites sent Miyetu's younger brother Yifu to lead the survivors back to their country.

sentences.zh: 伊匐擊柔然可汗婆羅門，大破之，婆羅門帥十部落詣涼州，請降於魏，柔然餘眾數萬相帥迎阿那瑰，阿那瑰啟稱：「本國大亂，姓姓別居，迭相抄掠。

translations.literal: Yifu attacked the Rouran khan Borumen and routed him severely; Borumen led ten tribes to Liangzhou to request surrender to Wei; tens of thousands of remaining Rouran, each leading one another, welcomed Anagui; Anagui memorialized saying: "Our state is in great disorder; clans live apart and seize from one another in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu attacked the Rouran khan Borumen and crushed him; Borumen led ten tribes to Liangzhou to surrender to Northern Wei; tens of thousands of remaining Rouran went out to welcome Anagui; Anagui memorialized: "Our country is in great turmoil; clans live apart and raid one another in turn.

sentences.zh: 當今北人鵠望待拯，乞依前恩賜，給臣精兵一萬，送臣磧北，撫定荒民。」

translations.literal: Now the northerners crane their necks awaiting rescue; I beg according to your former grace to grant me ten thousand picked troops, send me north of the desert, and settle the wild peoples."
translations.idiomatic: The northerners now crane their necks awaiting deliverance; I beg, as in your former kindness, to grant me ten thousand elite troops, send me north of the desert, and pacify the frontier peoples."

sentences.zh: 詔付中書門下博議，涼州刺史袁翻以為：「自國家都洛以來，蠕蠕、高車迭相吞噬。

translations.literal: An edict ordered broad discussion at the Secretariat and Chancellery; Liangzhou governor Yuan Fan held: "Since the state moved its capital to Luoyang, Rouran and Gaoche have devoured each other in turn.
translations.idiomatic: An edict referred the matter for broad discussion at the Secretariat and Chancellery; Liangzhou governor Yuan Fan argued: "Since the court moved the capital to Luoyang, Rouran and Gaoche have swallowed each other in turn.

sentences.zh: 始則蠕蠕授首，既而高車被擒。

translations.literal: At first Rouran offered their heads; afterward Gaoche was captured.
translations.idiomatic: At first Rouran submitted; then Gaoche was taken.

sentences.zh: 今高車自奮於衰微之中，克雪仇恥，誠由種類繁多，終不能相滅。

translations.literal: Now Gaoche has roused itself within decline and weakness and was able to avenge its shame—truly because their kinds are numerous, in the end they cannot destroy each other.
translations.idiomatic: Now Gaoche has revived from weakness and wiped away its shame—truly because their peoples are many, they can never wholly destroy one another.

sentences.zh: 自二虎交鬥，邊境無塵數十年矣，此中國之利也。

translations.literal: Since the two tigers fought each other, the borderlands have been without dust for decades—this is China's advantage.
translations.idiomatic: While the two tigers fought, the frontier was untroubled for decades—that was China's gain.

sentences.zh: 今蠕蠕兩主相繼歸誠，雖戎狄禽獸，終無純固之節，然存亡繼絕，帝王本務。

translations.literal: Now two Rouran lords in succession have come in good faith; though barbarians are like birds and beasts and in the end lack pure constancy, yet preserving the dying and continuing the cut off is the emperor's fundamental task.
translations.idiomatic: Now two Rouran rulers have submitted in succession; though barbarians are fickle, preserving the dying and continuing the cut off is an emperor's first duty.

sentences.zh: 若棄而不受，則虧我大德；

translations.literal: If we abandon them and do not accept them, we diminish our great virtue;
translations.idiomatic: If we reject them, we impair our great virtue;

sentences.zh: 若納而撫養，則損我資儲；

translations.literal: if we receive and nurture them, we deplete our stores;
translations.idiomatic: if we take them in and support them, we drain our resources;

sentences.zh: 或全徙內地，則非直其情不願，亦恐終為後患，劉、石是也。

translations.literal: or if we move them entirely into the interior, not only is that against their wishes, we also fear they will in the end become a later calamity—as with the Liu and Shi.
translations.idiomatic: or if we relocate them wholesale inland, they will not only resent it but may become a future scourge, as with the Liu and Shi.

sentences.zh: 且蠕蠕尚存，則高車有內顧之憂，未暇窺窬上國；

translations.literal: Moreover, while Rouran still exists, Gaoche has worry about looking back within and has no leisure to peep at our state;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, while Rouran survives, Gaoche must watch its rear and has no leisure to eye our realm;

sentences.zh: 若其全滅，則高車跋扈之勢，豈易可知！

translations.literal: if they are wholly destroyed, then Gaoche's overbearing momentum—how easily known!
translations.idiomatic: if Rouran is wiped out, Gaoche's arrogant strength—who can easily gauge it!

sentences.zh: 今蠕蠕雖亂而部落猶眾，處處棋布，以望舊主，高車雖強，未能盡服也。

translations.literal: Now though Rouran is chaotic its tribes are still numerous, scattered everywhere like chess pieces awaiting the old lord; though Gaoche is strong, it cannot make them all submit.
translations.idiomatic: Though Rouran is in disorder its tribes remain numerous, spread like chess pieces awaiting their old lord; Gaoche is strong but cannot subdue them all.

sentences.zh: 愚謂蠕蠕二主並宜存之，居阿那瑰於東，處婆羅門於西，分其降民，各有攸屬。

translations.literal: I deem both Rouran lords should be preserved—place Anagui in the east and Borumen in the west, divide their surrendering peoples, each with its proper allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that both Rouran rulers should be kept—set Anagui in the east and Borumen in the west, divide their submitted peoples, each with its proper master.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰所居非所經見，不敢臆度；

translations.literal: Anagui's dwelling place I have not seen and dare not presume to judge;
translations.idiomatic: I have not seen where Anagui should dwell and dare not guess;

sentences.zh: 婆羅門請修西海故城以處之。

translations.literal: Borumen asks to repair the old Western Sea city to house him.
translations.idiomatic: Borumen asks to rebuild the old Western Sea city to settle him.

sentences.zh: 西海在酒泉之北，去高車所居金山千餘里，實北虜往來之衝要，土地沃衍，大宜耕稼。

translations.literal: The Western Sea is north of Jiuquan, more than a thousand li from Jinshan where Gaoche dwells—a true thoroughfare for northern barbarians coming and going; the land is rich and spreading, greatly fit for farming.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Sea lies north of Jiuquan, over a thousand li from Jinshan where Gaoche live—a key corridor for northern peoples; the soil is fertile and excellent for agriculture.

sentences.zh: 宜遣一良將，配以兵仗，監護婆羅門。

translations.literal: One good general should be sent, provided with arms, to guard and oversee Borumen.
translations.idiomatic: A capable general should be sent with arms to guard Borumen.

sentences.zh: 因令屯田，以省轉輸之勞。

translations.literal: Order garrison farming thereby to save the labor of transport.
translations.idiomatic: Have troops farm there to spare the cost of supply convoys.

sentences.zh: 其北則臨大磧，野獸所聚，使蠕蠕射獵，彼此相資，足以自固。

translations.literal: To its north lies the great desert where beasts gather—let Rouran hunt by bow; each side supporting the other is enough for self-security.
translations.idiomatic: To the north lies the great desert where game abounds—let Rouran hunt there; mutual support will make them secure.

sentences.zh: 外以輔蠕蠕之微弱，內亦防高車之畔換，此安邊保塞之長計也。

translations.literal: Outwardly to assist Rouran's weakness, inwardly also to guard against Gaoche's rebellion—this is the long plan for securing the border and protecting the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly this aids weak Rouran; inwardly it checks Gaoche revolt—the sound long-term plan for securing the frontier.

sentences.zh: 若婆羅門能收離聚散，復興其國者，漸令北轉，徙度流沙，則是我之外籓，高車勍敵，西北之虞，可以無慮。

translations.literal: If Borumen can gather the scattered and restore his state, gradually order him to turn north and migrate across the flowing sands—then he will be our outer vassal; with Gaoche a strong foe, northwest worries can be set aside.
translations.idiomatic: If Borumen can rally the scattered and revive his state, gradually move him north across the desert—then he becomes our outer vassal, and with Gaoche as a strong enemy to the northwest we need not worry.

sentences.zh: 如其奸回返覆，不過為逋逃之寇，於我何損哉！」

translations.literal: If he is treacherous and turns back, he is no more than a fugitive raider—what harm to us!
translations.idiomatic: If he proves treacherous, he is only a runaway bandit—what loss to us!

sentences.zh: 朝議是之。

translations.literal: The court discussion approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted his view.

sentences.zh: 九月，柔然可汗俟匿伐詣懷朔鎮請兵，且迎阿那瑰。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the Rouran khan Houniifa went to Huaishuo garrison to request troops and also to welcome Anagui.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Rouran khan Houniifa came to Huaishuo garrison to ask for troops and to receive Anagui.

sentences.zh: 俟匿伐，阿那瑰之兄也。

translations.literal: Houniifa was Anagui's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Houniifa was Anagui's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，錄尚書事高陽王雍等奏：「懷朔鎮北吐若奚泉，原野平沃，請置阿那瑰於吐若奚泉，婆羅門於故西海郡，令各帥部落，收集離散。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: Supervisor of the Secretariat Gao Yang Wang Yong and others memorialized: "North of Huaishuo garrison is Turuo Xi spring; the plains are level and fertile—request placing Anagui at Turuo Xi spring and Borumen in the old Western Sea commandery, each to lead tribes and gather the scattered.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Supervisor of the Secretariat Prince Yong of Gaoyang and others memorialized: "North of Huaishuo garrison lies Turuo Xi spring, with level fertile plains—we ask that Anagui be placed at Turuo Xi spring and Borumen in the old Western Sea commandery, each to lead his tribes and gather the dispersed.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰所居既在境外，宜少優遣，婆羅門不得比之。

translations.literal: Since Anagui's dwelling is beyond the border, he should receive somewhat preferential dispatch; Borumen must not be equated with him.
translations.idiomatic: As Anagui's seat lies beyond the border, he should receive somewhat better support; Borumen must not be treated as his equal.

sentences.zh: 其婆羅門未降以前蠕蠕歸化者，宜悉令州鎮部送懷朔鎮以付阿那瑰。」

translations.literal: All Rouran who had submitted before Borumen's surrender should be ordered by provinces and garrisons to deliver them to Huaishuo garrison for Anagui.
translations.idiomatic: All Rouran who submitted before Borumen's surrender should be sent by provinces and garrisons to Huaishuo garrison for Anagui.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 十一月，癸丑，魏侍中、車騎大將軍侯剛加儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on guichou, Northern Wei's Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of Chariots and Cavalry Hou Gang was given Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on guichou, Northern Wei's Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of Chariots and Cavalry Hou Gang was made Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 魏以東益、南秦氐皆反，庚辰，以秦州刺史河間王琛為行台以討之。

translations.literal: Because Di in Eastern Yi and Southern Qin all rebelled, on gengchen Northern Wei made Qinzhou governor Prince Chen of Hejian mobile corps commissioner to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: As the Di of Eastern Yi and Southern Qin all rose, on gengchen Northern Wei made Qinzhou governor Prince Chen of Hejian mobile corps commissioner to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 琛恃劉騰之勢，貪暴無所畏忌，大為氐所敗。

translations.literal: Chen relied on Liu Teng's power, was greedy and violent without fear, and was greatly defeated by the Di.
translations.idiomatic: Chen leaned on Liu Teng's backing, plundered without restraint, and suffered a major defeat at the hands of the Di.

sentences.zh: 中尉彈奏，會赦，除名，尋復王爵。

translations.literal: The Chief Commandant impeached him; an amnesty coincided; his name was struck; soon his princely rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Commandant impeached him; an amnesty intervened and he was struck from the rolls, but soon his princely title was restored.

sentences.zh: 魏以安西將軍元洪超兼尚書行台，詣敦煌安置柔然婆羅門。

translations.literal: Northern Wei made General Who Pacifies the West Yuan Hongchao concurrent Mobile Corps Director of the Secretariat and sent him to Dunhuang to settle the Rouran Borumen.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei made General Who Pacifies the West Yuan Hongchao concurrent mobile corps Director of the Secretariat and sent him to Dunhuang to settle the Rouran ruler Borumen.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝五普通三年（

translations.literal: Martial Emperor Gaozu, fifth year of Putong (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang, fifth year of Putong (

sentences.zh: 壬寅，公元五二二年）

translations.literal: renyin, corresponding to 522 CE)
translations.idiomatic: renyin, corresponding to 522 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，庚子，以尚書令袁昂為中書監，吳郡太守王暕為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, gengzi: Yuan Ang, Director of the Secretariat, was made Supervisor of the Secretariat; Wang Yan, governor of Wu commandery, was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on gengzi, Director of the Secretariat Yuan Ang was made Supervisor of the Secretariat and Wu commandery governor Wang Yan was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，魏主耕籍田。

translations.literal: On xinhai, the Wei ruler plowed the altar fields.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai the Northern Wei emperor plowed the sacred fields.

sentences.zh: 魏宋雲與惠生自洛陽西行四千里，至赤嶺，乃出魏境，又西行，再期，至乾羅國而還。

translations.literal: Northern Wei's Song Yun and Huisheng went west from Luoyang four thousand li to Red Ridge, then left Wei territory; going west again two years, they reached the state of Ganluo and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei's Song Yun and Huisheng traveled west from Luoyang four thousand li to Red Ridge, then beyond Wei territory; after two more years west they reached Ganluo and returned.

sentences.zh: 二月，達洛陽，得佛經一百七十部。

translations.literal: In the second month they reached Luoyang, obtaining one hundred seventy sutra volumes.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month they reached Luoyang with one hundred seventy Buddhist sutras.

sentences.zh: 高車王伊匐遣使入貢於魏。

translations.literal: The Gaoche king Yifu sent envoys to present tribute to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoche king Yifu sent envoys to pay tribute to Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚辰，魏以伊匐為鎮西將軍、西海郡公、高車王。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, gengchen: Wei made Yifu General Who Guards the West, Duke of Western Sea commandery, and king of Gaoche.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on gengchen, Northern Wei made Yifu General Who Guards the West, Duke of Western Sea commandery, and king of Gaoche.

sentences.zh: 久之，伊匐與柔然戰，敗，其弟越居殺伊匐自立。

translations.literal: After a long while Yifu fought Rouran, was defeated, and his younger brother Yueju killed Yifu and established himself.
translations.idiomatic: After some time Yifu fought Rouran, was defeated, and his younger brother Yueju killed him and seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬辰朔，日有食之，既。

translations.literal: Fifth month, first day of renchen cycle: there was an eclipse of the sun; it was total.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the first day of the renchen cycle, there was a total solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，大赦。

translations.literal: On guisi, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi there was a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，甲午，領軍將軍始興忠武王憺卒。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month, jiawu: General of the Guards, Loyal Martial King of Shixing Dan, died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on jiawu, General of the Guards, Loyal Martial King of Shixing Xiao Dan, died.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，魏主祀圜丘。

translations.literal: On yisi, the Wei ruler sacrificed at the Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi the Northern Wei emperor sacrificed at the Round Mound.

sentences.zh: 初，魏世宗以《玄始歷》浸疏，命更造新歷。

translations.literal: Initially Emperor Shizong of Wei, because the Xuanshi Calendar had grown gradually loose, ordered a new calendar created.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Xiaoming of Northern Wei, finding the Xuanshi Calendar increasingly inaccurate, ordered a new calendar drafted.

sentences.zh: 至是，著作郎崔光表取蕩寇將軍張龍祥等九家所上歷，候驗得失，合為一歷，以壬子為元，應魏之水德，命曰《正光歷》。

translations.literal: At this time Compiler Cui Guang memorialized taking the calendars submitted by nine houses including Bandit-Suppressing General Zhang Longxiang, testing gains and losses, merging into one calendar with renzi as origin matching Wei's water virtue, named the Zhengguang Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Now Compiler Cui Guang memorialized adopting calendars from nine submitters including Bandit-Suppressing General Zhang Longxiang, testing them, and combining them into one calendar with renzi as the epoch to match Northern Wei's water phase, named the Zhengguang Calendar.

sentences.zh: 丙午，初行《正光歷》，大赦。

translations.literal: On bingwu, the Zhengguang Calendar was first implemented; general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu the Zhengguang Calendar took effect and there was a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙酉，魏以車騎大將軍、尚書右僕射元欽為儀同三司，太保京兆王繼為太傅，司徒崔光為太保。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, yiyou: Wei made General of Chariots and Cavalry and Right Vice Director Yuan Qin Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes; Grand Tutor Prince Ji of Jingzhao was made Grand Mentor; Minister of Works Cui Guang was made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yiyou, Northern Wei made General of Chariots and Cavalry and Right Vice Director Yuan Qin Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes, Grand Tutor Prince Ji of Jingzhao Grand Mentor, and Minister of Works Cui Guang Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 初，太子統之未生也，上養臨川王宏之子正德為子。

translations.literal: Initially, before Crown Prince Tong was born, the emperor raised Linchuan King Hong's son Zhengde as his son.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, before Crown Prince Tong was born, the emperor had adopted Linchuan Prince Hong's son Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 正德少粗險，上即位，正德意望東宮。

translations.literal: Zhengde was coarse and dangerous in youth; when the emperor took the throne, Zhengde hoped for the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde had been rough and treacherous from youth; when the emperor acceded, Zhengde expected to become heir.

sentences.zh: 及太子統生，正德還本，賜爵西豐侯。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Tong was born, Zhengde returned to his original line and was granted the marquisate of Xifeng.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Tong was born, Zhengde reverted to his birth family and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xifeng.

sentences.zh: 正德怏怏不滿意，常蓄異謀。

translations.literal: Zhengde was discontent and resentful and constantly harbored strange designs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde brooded in dissatisfaction and constantly nursed rebellious schemes.

sentences.zh: 是歲，正德自黃門侍郎為輕車將軍，頃之，亡奔魏，自稱廢太子避禍而來。

translations.literal: That year Zhengde went from Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates to General of Light Chariots; soon he fled to Wei, calling himself the deposed crown prince fleeing disaster.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhengde rose from Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates to General of Light Chariots; soon he fled to Northern Wei, claiming to be the deposed crown prince escaping harm.

sentences.zh: 魏尚書左僕射蕭寶寅上表曰：「豈有伯為天子，父作揚州，棄彼密親，遠投它國！

translations.literal: Northern Wei Left Vice Director Xiao Baoyin memorialized: "How can there be an uncle as Son of Heaven and a father as Yangzhou prefect, yet abandon those close kin and flee far to another state!
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei Left Vice Director Xiao Baoyin memorialized: "When one's uncle is emperor and one's father governs Yangzhou, who abandons close kin to flee to a foreign state!

sentences.zh: 不如殺之。」

translations.literal: Better to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: He should be killed."

sentences.zh: 由是魏人待之甚薄，正德乃殺一小兒，稱為己子，遠營葬地；

translations.literal: Thereupon the men of Wei treated him very coldly; Zhengde then killed a small child, called him his own son, and far away prepared a burial ground;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Wei court treated him coldly; Zhengde killed a small boy, passed him off as his son, and prepared a distant grave;

sentences.zh: 魏人不疑，明年，復自魏逃歸。

translations.literal: the men of Wei did not suspect; the next year he again fled back from Wei.
translations.idiomatic: the Wei court suspected nothing; the next year he fled back from Wei again.

sentences.zh: 上泣而誨之，復其封爵。

translations.literal: The emperor wept while admonishing him and restored his rank and fief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept as he admonished him and restored his title and fief.

sentences.zh: 柔然阿那瑰求粟為種，魏與之萬石。

translations.literal: Rouran Anagui requested grain as seed; Wei gave him ten thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran's Anagui asked for grain as seed stock; Northern Wei gave him ten thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 婆羅門帥部落叛魏，亡歸厭噠。

translations.literal: Borumen led his tribes in rebellion against Wei and fled to join the Ephthalites.
translations.idiomatic: Borumen led his tribes in revolt against Northern Wei and fled to the Ephthalites.

sentences.zh: 魏以平西府長史代人費穆兼尚書右丞西北道行台，將兵討之，柔然遁去。

translations.literal: Wei made Chief Clerk of the Pacify-the-West headquarters, the Dai man Fei Mu, concurrent Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and Northwest Route mobile corps commissioner, led troops against him; Rouran fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei made chief clerk of the Pacify-the-West headquarters, the Dai officer Fei Mu, concurrent Right Vice Director and Northwest Route mobile corps commissioner, and sent troops against him; the Rouran fled.

sentences.zh: 穆謂諸將曰：「戎狄之性，見敵即走，乘虛復出，若不使之破膽，終恐疲於奔命。」

translations.literal: Mu said to the generals: "The nature of the Rong and Di is to flee on seeing the enemy and emerge again when there is an opening—unless we break their spirit, in the end we will wear ourselves out in constant pursuit."
translations.idiomatic: Mu told his generals: "Barbarians flee at sight of the enemy and strike again when they see an opening—unless we break their nerve we shall wear ourselves out chasing them."

sentences.zh: 乃簡練精騎，伏於山谷，以步兵之羸者為外營，柔然果至；

translations.literal: He then picked elite cavalry and hid in a valley, using weak infantry as the outer camp; Rouran indeed came;
translations.idiomatic: He then selected elite cavalry and hid in a valley, posting weak infantry as an outer camp; the Rouran came as expected;

sentences.zh: 奮擊，大破之。

translations.literal: they struck fiercely and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: and a fierce attack routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 婆羅門為涼州軍所擒，送洛陽。

translations.literal: Borumen was captured by Liangzhou troops and sent to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Borumen was captured by Liangzhou forces and sent to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝五普通四年（

translations.literal: Martial Emperor Gaozu, sixth year of Putong (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang, sixth year of Putong (

sentences.zh: 癸卯，公元五二三年）

translations.literal: guimao, corresponding to 523 CE)
translations.idiomatic: guimao, corresponding to 523 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛卯，上祀南郊，大赦。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, xinmao: the emperor sacrificed at the Southern Suburb; general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on xinmao, the emperor sacrificed at the Southern Suburb and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 丙午，祀明堂。

translations.literal: On bingwu, sacrificed at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu he sacrificed at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙亥，耕藉田。

translations.literal: Second month, yihai: plowed the altar fields.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yihai, he plowed the sacred fields.

sentences.zh: 柔然大饑，阿那瑰帥其眾入魏境，表求賑給。

translations.literal: Rouran suffered great famine; Anagui led his multitude into Wei territory and memorialized seeking relief.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran suffered a great famine; Anagui led his people into Northern Wei territory and petitioned for relief.

sentences.zh: 己亥，魏以尚書左丞元孚為行台尚書，持節撫諭柔然。

translations.literal: On jihai, Wei made Left Vice Director Yuan Fu mobile corps Director of the Secretariat with staff of authority to soothe Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Northern Wei made Left Vice Director Yuan Fu mobile corps Director of the Secretariat with credentials to pacify the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 孚，譚之孫也。

translations.literal: Fu was Tan's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was a grandson of Tan.

sentences.zh: 將行，表陳便宜，以為：「蠕蠕久來強大，昔在代京，常為重備。

translations.literal: Before departing, he memorialized practical measures, holding: "Rouran has long been powerful; formerly at the capital in Dai it was heavily garrisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving he submitted recommendations, arguing: "Rouran has long been strong; when the capital was at Dai it was heavily guarded against them.

sentences.zh: 今天祚大魏，使彼自亂亡，稽首請服。

translations.literal: Today Heaven's mandate is on great Wei; they disorder themselves to destruction and bow requesting submission.
translations.idiomatic: Now Heaven favors great Wei; they have ruined themselves and bow in submission.

sentences.zh: 朝廷鳩其散亡，禮送令返，宜因此時善思遠策。

translations.literal: The court has gathered their scattered and dying, courteously sent them to return—the court should at this time think well on far-reaching policy.
translations.idiomatic: The court has gathered their scattered survivors and courteously sent them home—we should now devise a far-sighted policy.

sentences.zh: 昔漢宣之世，呼韓款塞，漢遣董忠、韓昌領邊郡士馬送出朔方，因留衛助。

translations.literal: In Han Xuandi's time Huhanye opened the passes; Han sent Dong Zhong and Han Chang leading border commandery troops and horses to escort him out through Shuofang and left guards to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan of Han, Huhanye came to the passes in friendship; Han sent Dong Zhong and Han Chang with border troops and horses to escort him out through Shuofang and left guards to help him.

sentences.zh: 又，光武時亦使中郎將段彬置安集掾史，隨單于所在，參察動靜。

translations.literal: Also in Guangwu's time they sent Colonel of the Interior Duan Bin to place Pacification clerks following wherever the chanyu was, to observe movements.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Guangwu as well, Colonel Duan Bin was sent to place Pacification clerks wherever the chanyu went, to watch his movements.

sentences.zh: 今宜略依舊事，借其閒地，聽其田牧，粗置官屬，示相慰撫。

translations.literal: Now we should roughly follow old precedents, lend them vacant land, allow their farming and herding, broadly place officials, and show mutual reassurance.
translations.idiomatic: Now we should follow those precedents in broad outline: lend them spare land, let them farm and graze, place officials in basic posts, and show reassuring oversight.

sentences.zh: 嚴戒邊兵，因令防察，使親不至矯詐，疏不容反叛，最策之得者也。」

translations.literal: Strictly warn the border troops, and thereby order surveillance, so that intimacy does not reach to pretense and fraud, and laxness does not allow rebellion—this is the most successful of policies."
translations.idiomatic: Keep border troops under strict discipline and surveillance, so favor never breeds deceit and negligence never allows revolt—that is the soundest policy."

sentences.zh: 魏人不從。

translations.literal: The Wei people did not follow [it].
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei court did not adopt his advice.

sentences.zh: 柔然俟匿伐入朝於魏。

translations.literal: The Rouran Houniifa came to court at Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran khan Houniifa came to the Northern Wei court.

sentences.zh: 三月，魏司空劉騰卒。

translations.literal: In the third month, Wei Minister of Works Liu Teng died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Northern Wei Minister of Works Liu Teng died.

sentences.zh: 宦官為騰義息重服者四十餘人，衰絰送葬者以百數，朝貴送葬者塞路滿野。

translations.literal: More than forty eunuchs wore heavy mourning as Liu Teng's adoptive sons; those in hemp and sending off the burial numbered in the hundreds; court nobles attending the funeral filled the roads and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: More than forty eunuchs wore full mourning as Liu Teng's adopted sons; mourners in hemp numbered in the hundreds; nobles at the funeral clogged the roads and fields.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，魏元孚持白虎幡勞阿那瑰於柔玄、懷荒二鎮之間。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Wei Yuan Fu bore the white tiger banner to reward Anagui between the Rouxuan and Huaihuang garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Yuan Fu of Northern Wei carried the white tiger banner to reward Anagui between the Rouxuan and Huaihuang garrisons.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰眾號三十萬，陰有異志，遂拘留孚，載以轀車。

translations.literal: Anagui's forces claimed three hundred thousand; secretly he had other intentions; he then detained Fu and carried him in a curtained carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui's followers claimed three hundred thousand men; he secretly harbored other designs, detained Fu, and carried him in a covered carriage.

sentences.zh: 每集其眾，坐孚東廂，稱為行台，甚加禮敬。

translations.literal: Whenever he gathered his multitude he seated Fu in the east wing, called him the mobile desk, and greatly honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he assembled his followers he seated Fu in the east wing, styled him the mobile headquarters, and treated him with great respect.

sentences.zh: 引兵而南，所過剽掠，至平城，乃聽孚還。

translations.literal: He led troops south, plundering wherever he passed; reaching Pingcheng, he then allowed Fu to return.
translations.idiomatic: He marched south, looting along the way; only when he reached Pingcheng did he let Fu go home.

sentences.zh: 有司奏孚辱命，抵罪。

translations.literal: The authorities memorialized that Fu had disgraced his commission; he was punished.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities reported that Fu had failed his mission, and he was punished.

sentences.zh: 甲申，魏遣尚書令李崇、左僕射元纂帥騎十萬擊柔然。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Wei sent Secretary Director Li Chong and Left Vice Director Yuan Zuan leading one hundred thousand cavalry to attack Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Northern Wei sent Secretary Director Li Chong and Left Vice Director Yuan Zuan with one hundred thousand horsemen against the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰聞之，驅良民二千、公私馬牛羊數十萬北遁，崇追之三千餘里，不及而還。

translations.literal: Anagui heard of it, drove two thousand good civilians and hundreds of thousands of public and private horses, cattle, and sheep north to flee; Chong pursued over three thousand li, did not catch up, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Anagui drove off two thousand civilians and vast herds of public and private livestock northward; Chong pursued more than three thousand li, failed to overtake him, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 纂使鎧曹參軍於謹帥騎二千追柔然，至郁對原，前後十七戰，屢破之。

translations.literal: Zuan sent Armor Bureau staff officer Yu Jin leading two thousand cavalry in pursuit of Rouran; reaching the Yudui plains, they fought seventeen battles before and after and repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan sent Armor Bureau staff officer Yu Jin with two thousand horsemen after the Rouran; on the Yudui plains they fought seventeen engagements and repeatedly routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 謹，忠之從曾孫也，性深沉，有識量，涉獵經史。

translations.literal: Jin was the great-great-grandson of Zhong; his nature was deep and reserved, he had judgment, and he ranged through the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was a great-great-grandson of Yu Zhong—reserved and thoughtful, widely read in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 少時，屏居閭裡，不求仕進，或勸之仕，謹曰：「州郡之職，昔人所鄙；

translations.literal: In youth he lived in seclusion in his village and did not seek advancement; someone urged him to serve; Jin said: "State and commandery posts are what men of old despised;
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he lived quietly in his village and refused office; when urged to serve he said, "Provincial and commandery posts were scorned by the ancients;

sentences.zh: 台鼎之位，須待時來。」

translations.literal: Tripod-and-caldrons rank must await the time to come."
translations.idiomatic: the highest offices must wait their proper season."

sentences.zh: 纂聞其名而辟之。

translations.literal: Zuan heard his name and recruited him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zuan heard of him and summoned him to service.

sentences.zh: 後帥輕騎出塞覘候，屬鐵勒數千騎奄至，謹以眾寡不敵，退必不免，乃散其眾騎，使匿叢薄之間，又遺人升山指麾，若部分軍眾者。

translations.literal: Later, leading light cavalry out of the pass to reconnoiter, it happened that several thousand Tiele horsemen arrived suddenly; Jin knew he was outmatched and that retreat would not escape; he therefore scattered his cavalry and had them hide in thickets, and also sent men up a hill to direct as if deploying troops.
translations.idiomatic: Later, leading light cavalry beyond the pass on reconnaissance, he was suddenly surrounded by several thousand Tiele horsemen; seeing he was outnumbered and could not escape by flight, he scattered his men to hide in brush and sent others up a hill to gesture as though marshaling a large force.

sentences.zh: 鐵勒望見，雖疑有伏兵，自恃其眾，進軍逼謹。

translations.literal: The Tiele saw this; though they suspected an ambush, trusting their numbers they advanced to press Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiele saw this; though they suspected an ambush, they trusted their numbers and pressed forward against Jin.

sentences.zh: 謹以常乘駿馬，一紫一騧，鐵勒所識，乃使二人各乘一馬突陣而出，鐵勒以為謹也，爭逐之；

translations.literal: Jin regularly rode excellent horses, one purple and one piebald, which the Tiele knew; he therefore had two men each ride one horse break through the formation; the Tiele thought it was Jin and scrambled to pursue;
translations.idiomatic: Jin habitually rode two fine horses, one purple and one piebald, well known to the Tiele; he had two men each mount one and charge through the enemy lines; the Tiele took them for Jin and raced after them;

sentences.zh: 謹帥餘軍擊其追騎，鐵勒遂走，謹因得入塞。

translations.literal: Jin led the remaining army to strike their pursuit cavalry; the Tiele then fled, and Jin thereby entered the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Jin then struck their pursuers with the rest of his force; the Tiele fled, and he made it back inside the pass.

sentences.zh: 李崇長史巨鹿魏蘭根說崇曰：「昔緣邊初置諸鎮，地廣人稀，或征發中原強宗子弟，或國之肺腑，寄以爪牙。

translations.literal: Li Chong's chief clerk Wei Langen of Julu advised Chong, saying: "Formerly when the border garrisons were first established, the land was broad and people sparse; sometimes strong clan youths of the central plains were conscripted, or the state's vitals were entrusted as claws and fangs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong's chief clerk Wei Langen of Julu urged him: "When the frontier garrisons were first set up, the land was vast and sparsely peopled; sometimes powerful families of the central plains were drafted, sometimes imperial kin were posted as the dynasty's claws and fangs.

sentences.zh: 中年以來，有司號為『府戶』，役同廝養，官婚班齒，致失清流，而本來族類，各居榮顯，顧瞻彼此，理當憤怨。

translations.literal: From mid-dynasty on, the authorities called them 'garrison households'; their service was the same as servants; official marriage by seniority caused loss of elite standing, while their original clan types each held glory and eminence—looking at each other, resentment was natural.
translations.idiomatic: In later years the authorities labeled them 'garrison households': they served like bondsmen, and official marriages by seniority stripped them of elite status while their original kin still held honor—no wonder they resented what they saw.

sentences.zh: 宜改鎮立州，分置郡縣，凡是府戶，悉免為民，入仕次敘，一准其舊，文武兼用，威恩並施。

translations.literal: The garrisons should be changed to establish provinces, with commanderies and counties divided and placed; all garrison households should be entirely freed as commoners, enter office in sequence, on one standard with the old, civil and military both used, authority and kindness both applied.
translations.idiomatic: Convert the garrisons into provinces with proper commanderies and counties; free all garrison households as ordinary subjects, restore their right to office by the old rules, employ both civil and military means, and combine stern authority with kindness.

sentences.zh: 此計若行，國家庶無北顧之慮矣。」

translations.literal: If this plan is carried out, the state will probably have no worry of looking north."
translations.idiomatic: If this is done, the court may cease to fear trouble from the north."

sentences.zh: 崇為之奏聞，事寢，不報。

translations.literal: Chong submitted it upward; the matter was shelved, with no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Chong memorialized the throne, but the proposal was shelved without response.

sentences.zh: 初，元義既幽胡太后，常入直於魏主所居殿側，曲盡佞媚，帝由是寵信之。

translations.literal: Initially, Yuan Yi having imprisoned Empress Dowager Hu, constantly entered duty beside the Wei emperor's residence hall, fully using flattery; the emperor thereby favored and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Yi had imprisoned Empress Dowager Hu, he constantly attended the emperor in the palace halls and flattered him to the full; the emperor came to favor and trust him.

sentences.zh: 義出入禁中，恆令勇士持兵以自先後。

translations.literal: When Yi entered and left the forbidden precinct he always had brave men hold weapons before and behind himself.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yi entered or left the palace he had armed guards before and behind him.

sentences.zh: 時出休於千秋門外，施木欄楯，使腹心防守以備竊發，士民求見者，遙對之而已。

translations.literal: When going out to rest outside the Qianqiu Gate, he set wooden palisades and had trusted men defend against surprise attack; commoners seeking audience only faced him from afar.
translations.idiomatic: When he rested outside the Qianqiu Gate he erected wooden barriers and posted trusted guards against assassination; petitioners were kept at a distance.

sentences.zh: 其始執政之時，矯情自飾，以謙勤接物，時事得失，頗以關懷。

translations.literal: When he first held power he feigned sentiment and adorned himself, receiving people with humility and diligence; gains and losses of current affairs he somewhat cared about.
translations.idiomatic: At first he played the modest, diligent minister and took some interest in public affairs.

sentences.zh: 既得志，遂自驕愎，嗜酒好色，貪吝寶賄，與奪任情，紀綱壞亂。

translations.literal: Having got his wish, he then became proud and obstinate, addicted to wine and lust for women, greedy and grasping bribes, giving and taking at whim; regulations were ruined and disordered.
translations.idiomatic: Once secure in power he grew arrogant and wilful, given to wine and women, greedy for bribes, and lawless in appointments; government discipline collapsed.

sentences.zh: 父京兆王繼尤貪縱，與其妻子各受賂遺，請屬有司，莫敢違者。

translations.literal: His father, Prince Ji of Jingzhao, was especially greedy and unrestrained; with his wife and children each received bribes, and requests to the authorities—none dared disobey.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Prince Ji of Jingzhao, was even more grasping; he and his family took bribes freely, and no official dared refuse their requests.

sentences.zh: 乃致郡縣小吏亦不得公選，牧、守、令、長率皆貪污之人。

translations.literal: Thus even commandery and county petty clerks could not be publicly selected; regional inspectors, prefects, and magistrates were mostly all corrupt men.
translations.idiomatic: Even petty clerks were no longer chosen openly; most governors, prefects, and magistrates were corrupt.

sentences.zh: 由是百姓困窮，人人思亂。

translations.literal: By this the common people were impoverished; everyone thought of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The people were driven to destitution, and rebellion was on every mind.

sentences.zh: 武衛將軍於景，忠之弟也，謀廢義，義黜為懷荒鎮將。

translations.literal: Martial Guards General Yu Jing, Zhong's younger brother, plotted to depose Yi; Yi demoted him to commander of Huaihuang garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Martial Guards General Yu Jing, younger brother of Yu Zhong, plotted to remove Yi; Yi banished him to command Huaihuang garrison.

sentences.zh: 及柔然入寇，鎮民請糧，景不肯給，鎮民不勝忿，遂反，執景，殺之。

translations.literal: When Rouran invaded, the garrison people requested grain; Jing refused to give it; the garrison people could not bear their rage, then rebelled, seized Jing, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran raided, the garrison sought grain; Jing refused; the troops, enraged, rose up, seized him, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，沃野鎮民破六韓拔陵聚眾反，殺鎮將，改元真王，諸鎮華、夷之民往往響應。

translations.literal: Before long, Woye garrison people Buliugu Baleng gathered the masses and rebelled, killed the garrison commander, changed the era name to True King; people of the various garrisons, Chinese and barbarian, often responded.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Buliugu Baleng of Woye garrison rallied a revolt, killed the commander, and declared the era name True King; Chinese and non-Chinese across the garrisons joined him in droves.

sentences.zh: 拔陵引兵南侵，遣別帥衛可孤圍武川鎮，又攻懷朔鎮。

translations.literal: Baleng led troops south to invade and sent a separate commander, Wei Kehu, to besiege Wuchuan garrison and also attack Huaishuo garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Baleng marched south and sent Wei Kehu to besiege Wuchuan while also striking Huaishuo.

sentences.zh: 尖山賀拔度拔及其三子允、勝、岳皆有材勇，懷朔鎮將楊鈞擢度拔為統軍、三子為軍主以拒之。

translations.literal: Helü Tabo of Jianshan and his three sons Yun, Sheng, and Yue all had talent and courage; Huaishuo garrison commander Yang Jun promoted Tabo as commander-in-chief and the three sons as army commanders to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Helü Tabo of Jianshan and his sons Yun, Sheng, and Yue were all brave and capable; Yang Jun, commander of Huaishuo, made Tabo commander-in-chief and his sons army chiefs to resist the rebels.

sentences.zh: 魏景明之初，世宗命宦者白整為高祖及文昭高後鑿二佛龕於龍門山，皆高百尺。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wei Jingming, Shizong ordered the eunuch Bai Zheng to carve two Buddha niches for Gaozu and Empress Wen Zhao at Longmen mountain, each a hundred chi high.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingming era Emperor Shizong had the eunuch Bai Zheng carve two hundred-chi Buddha niches at Longmen for Emperor Gaozu and Empress Wen Zhao.

sentences.zh: 永平中，劉騰復為世宗鑿一龕，至是二十四年，凡用十八萬二千餘工，而未成。

translations.literal: In Yongping, Liu Teng again carved one niche for Shizong; by now twenty-four years had passed, using in all over one hundred eighty-two thousand workers, yet it was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongping era Liu Teng added another niche for Shizong; twenty-four years on, more than 182,000 laborers had been used and the work was still unfinished.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛亥，魏詔：「見在朝官，依令七十合解者，可給本官半祿，以終其身。」

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinhai, a Wei edict: "Present court officials who per statute at seventy should retire may be given half the salary of their original office to the end of their lives."
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinhai Northern Wei decreed: "Serving officials who by law should retire at seventy may receive half their former salary for life."

sentences.zh: 九月，魏詔侍中、太尉汝南王悅入居門下，與丞相高陽王雍參決尚書奏事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, a Wei edict: Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant Prince of Runan Yue to enter and reside at the Gate Department, with Chancellor Prince of Gaoyang Yong jointly deciding Secretariat memorials.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Northern Wei ordered Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant Prince Yue of Runan to join the Gate Department and, with Chancellor Prince Yong of Gaoyang, decide Secretariat business.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，庚午，以中書監、中衛將軍袁昂為尚書令，即本號開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on gengwu, made Secretariat Supervisor and Central Guard General Yuan Ang Grand Secretary Director, with his original title made Advisor-in-Chief with the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on gengwu Yuan Ang was made Grand Secretary Director while retaining his posts as Secretariat Supervisor and Central Guard General and was given the Staff of Honor Equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 魏平恩文宣公崔光疾篤，魏主親撫視之，拜其子勵為齊州刺史，為之撤樂，罷游眺。

translations.literal: Wei Duke of Ping'en, the Cultured and Sagely, Cui Guang was gravely ill; the Wei emperor personally visited him, appointed his son Li Governor of Qi Province, and for him withdrew music and stopped excursions.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang, Duke of Ping'en, lay gravely ill; the Northern Wei emperor visited him in person, appointed his son Li governor of Qi province, and suspended music and outings for his sake.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，光卒，帝臨，哭之慟，為減常膳。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Guang died; the emperor came in person, wept bitterly, and reduced his regular meals.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou Guang died; the emperor attended the mourning, wept bitterly, and cut back his own table.

sentences.zh: 光寬和樂善，終日怡怡，未嘗忿恚。

translations.literal: Guang was genial and delighted in goodness, cheerful all day, and never angry.
translations.idiomatic: Guang was gentle and good-natured, cheerful all day, and never wrathful.

sentences.zh: 於忠、元義用事，以光舊德，皆尊敬之，事多資決，而不能救裴、郭、清河之死，時人比之張禹、胡廣。

translations.literal: When Yu Zhong and Yuan Yi held power, because of Guang's old virtue they all respected him and many affairs relied on his decisions; yet he could not save the deaths of Pei, Guo, and Qinghe; people of the time compared him to Zhang Yu and Hu Guang.
translations.idiomatic: While Yu Zhong and Yuan Yi were in power they respected Guang for his standing and often sought his counsel, yet he could not save Pei, Guo, or the Prince of Qinghe from death; contemporaries compared him to Zhang Yu and Hu Guang.

sentences.zh: 光且死，薦都官尚書賈思伯為侍講。

translations.literal: As Guang was about to die, he recommended Chief Judge of the Court Jia Sibai as lecturer accompanying the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Guang recommended Chief Judge Jia Sibai as the emperor's lecturer.

sentences.zh: 帝從思伯受《春秋》，思伯雖貴，傾身下士。

translations.literal: The emperor studied the 《Spring and Autumn》 from Sibai; Sibai, though noble, bent his person to treat gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor studied the 《Spring and Autumn》 under Sibai, who despite his rank humbled himself before scholars.

sentences.zh: 或問思伯曰：「公何以能不驕？」

translations.literal: Someone asked Sibai: "How can you, sir, not be proud?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Sibai, "How is it that you are never arrogant?"

sentences.zh: 思伯曰：「衰至便驕，何常之有！」

translations.literal: Sibai said: "When decline comes one becomes proud—how is that constant!"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "People grow proud only as they fade—what is constant about that!"

sentences.zh: 當時以為雅談。

translations.literal: People of the time regarded it as elegant talk.
translations.idiomatic: The remark was admired as a fine saying.

sentences.zh: 十一月，癸未朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on guiwei new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the guiwei new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，尚書左僕射王暕卒。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Left Vice Director Wang Yan died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen Left Vice Director Wang Yan died.

sentences.zh: 梁初唯揚、荊、郢、江、湘、梁、益七州用錢，交、廣用金銀，餘州雜以谷帛交易。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Liang, only Yang, Jing, Ying, Jiang, Xiang, Liang, and Yi seven provinces used coin; Jiao and Guang used gold and silver; the remaining provinces mixed grain and silk for trade.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Liang dynasty only seven provinces—Yang, Jing, Ying, Jiang, Xiang, Liang, and Yi—used coin; Jiao and Guang used gold and silver; elsewhere grain and cloth served as currency.

sentences.zh: 上乃鑄五銖錢，肉好周郭皆備。

translations.literal: The emperor then cast five-zhu coins, with rim, hole, and outer band all complete.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then cast five-zhu coins with full rims and outer bands.

sentences.zh: 別鑄無肉郭者，謂之「女錢」。

translations.literal: He separately cast ones without rim bands, calling them "female coins."
translations.idiomatic: He also minted coins without outer rims, called "female coins."

sentences.zh: 民間私用古錢交易，禁之不能止，乃議盡罷銅錢。

translations.literal: Among the people old coins were privately used in trade; prohibition could not stop it; they then discussed entirely abolishing copper coins.
translations.idiomatic: The people kept trading in old coins despite the ban; the court then debated abolishing copper currency altogether.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊午，始鑄鐵錢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on wuwu, they began casting iron coins.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wuwu, iron coins were first cast.

sentences.zh: 魏以汝南王悅為太保。

translations.literal: Wei made Prince of Runan Yue Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei made Prince Yue of Runan Grand Tutor.
